# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/yatrosci-special/0.1.0/src/yatrosci_special/lib.rs.html

# yatrosci_special/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! # SciRS Special Functions
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! Special mathematical functions for scientific computing,
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! providing functionality equivalent to `scipy.special`.
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//!
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! ## Overview
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//!
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! This crate provides:
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! - Gamma and related functions (gamma, lgamma, digamma, beta)
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! - Bessel functions (J, Y, I, K)
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! - Error functions (erf, erfc, erfinv)
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! - Airy functions
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! - Elliptic functions and integrals
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! - Hypergeometric functions
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! - Orthogonal polynomials (Legendre, Hermite, Laguerre, Chebyshev)
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! - Spherical harmonics
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! - Zeta and related functions
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//!
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! ## Example
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! ```rust,ignore
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! use yatrosci_special::{gamma, erf, bessel_j0, legendre_p};
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! // Gamma function
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! let g = gamma(5.0);  // = 4! = 24
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! // Error function
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! let e = erf(1.0);  // ≈ 0.8427
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! // Bessel function
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! let j0 = bessel_j0(1.0);  // ≈ 0.7652
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! ```
[33](https://docs.rs#33)
[34](https://docs.rs#34)#![warn(missing_docs)]
[35](https://docs.rs#35)#![warn(clippy::all)]
[36](https://docs.rs#36)
[37](https://docs.rs#37)use thiserror::Error;
[38](https://docs.rs#38)
[39](https://docs.rs#39)// Re-export core types
[40](https://docs.rs#40)pub use yatrosci_core::Float;
[41](https://docs.rs#41)
[42](https://docs.rs#42)// ============================================================================
[43](https://docs.rs#43)// ERROR TYPES
[44](https://docs.rs#44)// ============================================================================
[45](https://docs.rs#45)
[46](https://docs.rs#46)/// Errors in special function evaluation
[47](https://docs.rs#47)#[derive(Error, Debug)]
[48](https://docs.rs#48)pub enum SpecialError {
[49](https://docs.rs#49)    /// Domain error (function undefined for input)
[50](https://docs.rs#50)    #[error("Domain error: {0}")]
[51](https://docs.rs#51)    DomainError(String),
[52](https://docs.rs#52)
[53](https://docs.rs#53)    /// Convergence failure in iterative computation
[54](https://docs.rs#54)    #[error("Convergence failure: {0}")]
[55](https://docs.rs#55)    ConvergenceError(String),
[56](https://docs.rs#56)
[57](https://docs.rs#57)    /// Overflow or underflow
[58](https://docs.rs#58)    #[error("Numerical overflow/underflow: {0}")]
[59](https://docs.rs#59)    OverflowError(String),
[60](https://docs.rs#60)}
[61](https://docs.rs#61)
[62](https://docs.rs#62)/// Result type for special functions
[63](https://docs.rs#63)pub type SpecialResult<T> = Result<T, SpecialError>;
[64](https://docs.rs#64)
[65](https://docs.rs#65)// ============================================================================
[66](https://docs.rs#66)// GAMMA AND RELATED FUNCTIONS
[67](https://docs.rs#67)// ============================================================================
[68](https://docs.rs#68)
[69](https://docs.rs#69)/// Gamma function module
[70](https://docs.rs#70)pub mod gamma_funcs {
[71](https://docs.rs#71)
[72](https://docs.rs#72)    /// Compute the gamma function `Gamma(x)`.
[73](https://docs.rs#73)    ///
[74](https://docs.rs#74)    /// # Algoritmo
[75](https://docs.rs#75)    ///
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    /// ```text
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    /// \Gamma(x) = \int_0^\infty t^{x-1} e^{-t} dt
[78](https://docs.rs#78)    /// ```
[79](https://docs.rs#79)    /// Uses the Lanczos approximation internally via the `libm` crate.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)    ///
[81](https://docs.rs#81)    /// # Precisión numérica
[82](https://docs.rs#82)    ///
[83](https://docs.rs#83)    /// Relies on `libm::tgamma` which provides close to IEEE 754 double precision.
[84](https://docs.rs#84)    /// Returns `NaN` for non-positive integers.
[85](https://docs.rs#85)    ///
[86](https://docs.rs#86)    /// # Referencias
[87](https://docs.rs#87)    ///
[88](https://docs.rs#88)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §5.2.1.
[89](https://docs.rs#89)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[90](https://docs.rs#90)    /// - Abramowitz, M., & Stegun, I. A. (1964). *Handbook of Mathematical Functions*. §6.1.
[91](https://docs.rs#91)    ///
[92](https://docs.rs#92)    /// # Advertencias numéricas
[93](https://docs.rs#93)    ///
[94](https://docs.rs#94)    /// Has poles at non-positive integers where it returns `NaN` instead of infinity to avoid silent propagation of unbounded values.
[95](https://docs.rs#95)    pub fn gamma(x: f64) -> f64 {
[96](https://docs.rs#96)        if x <= 0.0 && x.floor() == x {
[97](https://docs.rs#97)            return f64::NAN; // Poles at non-positive integers
[98](https://docs.rs#98)        }
[99](https://docs.rs#99)
[100](https://docs.rs#100)        // Use libm's tgamma
[101](https://docs.rs#101)        libm::tgamma(x)
[102](https://docs.rs#102)    }
[103](https://docs.rs#103)
[104](https://docs.rs#104)    /// Compute the natural logarithm of the gamma function, `\ln(\Gamma(x))`.
[105](https://docs.rs#105)    ///
[106](https://docs.rs#106)    /// # Algoritmo
[107](https://docs.rs#107)    ///
[108](https://docs.rs#108)    /// Delegates to `libm::lgamma`.
[109](https://docs.rs#109)    ///
[110](https://docs.rs#110)    /// # Precisión numérica
[111](https://docs.rs#111)    ///
[112](https://docs.rs#112)    /// Avoids the overflow that would occur if computing `gamma(x).ln()` for large `x`.
[113](https://docs.rs#113)    ///
[114](https://docs.rs#114)    /// # Referencias
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    ///
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §5.2.2.
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[118](https://docs.rs#118)    pub fn lgamma(x: f64) -> f64 {
[119](https://docs.rs#119)        libm::lgamma(x)
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    }
[121](https://docs.rs#121)
[122](https://docs.rs#122)    /// Compute the sign of `gamma(x)`.
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    ///
[124](https://docs.rs#124)    /// # Algoritmo
[125](https://docs.rs#125)    ///
[126](https://docs.rs#126)    /// Returns a tuple `(lgamma(x), sign)` where `sign` is 1 or -1.
[127](https://docs.rs#127)    /// The sign is positive for `x > 0` and alternates between 1 and -1 for negative intervals.
[128](https://docs.rs#128)    ///
[129](https://docs.rs#129)    /// # Referencias
[130](https://docs.rs#130)    ///
[131](https://docs.rs#131)    /// - Abramowitz, M., & Stegun, I. A. (1964). *Handbook of Mathematical Functions*. §6.1.
[132](https://docs.rs#132)    pub fn lgamma_sign(x: f64) -> (f64, i32) {
[133](https://docs.rs#133)        let lg = lgm(x);
[134](https://docs.rs#134)        let sign = if x > 0.0 || x.floor() as i64 % 2 == 0 {
[135](https://docs.rs#135)            1
[136](https://docs.rs#136)        } else {
[137](https://docs.rs#137)            -1
[138](https://docs.rs#138)        };
[139](https://docs.rs#139)        (lg, sign)
[140](https://docs.rs#140)    }
[141](https://docs.rs#141)
[142](https://docs.rs#142)    fn lgm(x: f64) -> f64 {
[143](https://docs.rs#143)        libm::lgamma(x)
[144](https://docs.rs#144)    }
[145](https://docs.rs#145)
[146](https://docs.rs#146)    /// Compute the digamma function (psi function), `\psi(x)`.
[147](https://docs.rs#147)    ///
[148](https://docs.rs#148)    /// # Algoritmo
[149](https://docs.rs#149)    ///
[150](https://docs.rs#150)    /// ```text
[151](https://docs.rs#151)    /// \psi(x) = \frac{d}{dx} \ln(\Gamma(x)) = \frac{\Gamma'(x)}{\Gamma(x)}
[152](https://docs.rs#152)    /// ```
[153](https://docs.rs#153)    /// Uses asymptotic expansion for `x > 10`, recurrence relation for `x < 1`,
[154](https://docs.rs#154)    /// reflection formula for negative `x`, and series expansion otherwise.
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    ///
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    /// # Precisión numérica
[157](https://docs.rs#157)    ///
[158](https://docs.rs#158)    /// - Asymptotic expansion for large `x` uses Bernoulli numbers up to 6th order.
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    /// - Truncation at 100 iterations for series expansion.
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    ///
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    /// # Referencias
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    ///
[163](https://docs.rs#163)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §5.11.
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    /// - Abramowitz, M., & Stegun, I. A. (1964). *Handbook of Mathematical Functions*. Eq 6.3.18.
[166](https://docs.rs#166)    pub fn digamma(x: f64) -> f64 {
[167](https://docs.rs#167)        // Asymptotic expansion for large x
[168](https://docs.rs#168)        if x > 10.0 {
[169](https://docs.rs#169)            let inv_x = 1.0 / x;
[170](https://docs.rs#170)            let inv_x2 = inv_x * inv_x;
[171](https://docs.rs#171)            return x.ln() - 0.5 * inv_x - inv_x2 / 12.0 + inv_x2 * inv_x2 / 120.0
[172](https://docs.rs#172)                - inv_x2 * inv_x2 * inv_x2 / 252.0;
[173](https://docs.rs#173)        }
[174](https://docs.rs#174)
[175](https://docs.rs#175)        // Recurrence relation for small x
[176](https://docs.rs#176)        if x < 1.0 {
[177](https://docs.rs#177)            return digamma(x + 1.0) - 1.0 / x;
[178](https://docs.rs#178)        }
[179](https://docs.rs#179)
[180](https://docs.rs#180)        // Use reflection for negative x
[181](https://docs.rs#181)        if x < 0.0 && x.floor() != x {
[182](https://docs.rs#182)            return digamma(1.0 - x) - std::f64::consts::PI / (std::f64::consts::PI * x).tan();
[183](https://docs.rs#183)        }
[184](https://docs.rs#184)
[185](https://docs.rs#185)        // Series expansion
[186](https://docs.rs#186)        let mut result = -0.5772156649015329; // Euler-Mascheroni constant
[187](https://docs.rs#187)        for n in 1..100 {
[188](https://docs.rs#188)            let nf = n as f64;
[189](https://docs.rs#189)            result += 1.0 / nf - 1.0 / (nf + x - 1.0);
[190](https://docs.rs#190)        }
[191](https://docs.rs#191)
[192](https://docs.rs#192)        result
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    }
[194](https://docs.rs#194)
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    /// Compute the trigamma function, `\psi_1(x)`.
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    ///
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    /// # Algoritmo
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    ///
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    /// ```text
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    /// \psi_1(x) = \frac{d^2}{dx^2} \ln(\Gamma(x))
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    /// ```
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    /// Uses asymptotic expansion for `x > 10`, recurrence relation for `x < 1`,
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    /// and central finite difference derivative of digamma for intermediate values.
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    ///
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    /// # Precisión numérica
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    ///
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    /// Finite difference uses step `h = 1e-8`. This limits precision to approx `O(h^2) = 1e-16`, which is within double precision bounds.
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    ///
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    /// # Referencias
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    ///
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §5.15.
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    /// - Abramowitz, M., & Stegun, I. A. (1964). *Handbook of Mathematical Functions*. Eq 6.4.11.
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    pub fn trigamma(x: f64) -> f64 {
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        // Asymptotic expansion
[216](https://docs.rs#216)        if x > 10.0 {
[217](https://docs.rs#217)            let inv_x = 1.0 / x;
[218](https://docs.rs#218)            let inv_x2 = inv_x * inv_x;
[219](https://docs.rs#219)            return inv_x + 0.5 * inv_x2 + inv_x2 * inv_x / 6.0 - inv_x2 * inv_x2 * inv_x / 30.0;
[220](https://docs.rs#220)        }
[221](https://docs.rs#221)
[222](https://docs.rs#222)        // Recurrence relation
[223](https://docs.rs#223)        if x < 1.0 {
[224](https://docs.rs#224)            return trigamma(x + 1.0) + 1.0 / (x * x);
[225](https://docs.rs#225)        }
[226](https://docs.rs#226)
[227](https://docs.rs#227)        // Numerical derivative of digamma
[228](https://docs.rs#228)        let h = 1e-8;
[229](https://docs.rs#229)        (digamma(x + h) - digamma(x - h)) / (2.0 * h)
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    }
[231](https://docs.rs#231)
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    /// Compute the polygamma function of order `n`, `\psi_n(x)`.
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    ///
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    /// # Algoritmo
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    ///
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    /// ```text
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    /// \psi_n(x) = \frac{d^{n+1}}{dx^{n+1}} \ln(\Gamma(x))
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    /// ```
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    /// Resolves to analytical forms for `n=0` and `n=1`. For `n > 1`, uses numerical differentiation.
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    ///
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    /// # Precisión numérica
[242](https://docs.rs#242)    ///
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    /// Recursive finite differentiation uses `h = 1e-5`. Significant precision loss occurs for `n > 2`.
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    ///
[245](https://docs.rs#245)    /// # Referencias
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    ///
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §5.15.
[248](https://docs.rs#248)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    pub fn polygamma(n: usize, x: f64) -> f64 {
[250](https://docs.rs#250)        match n {
[251](https://docs.rs#251)            0 => digamma(x),
[252](https://docs.rs#252)            1 => trigamma(x),
[253](https://docs.rs#253)            _ => {
[254](https://docs.rs#254)                // Numerical differentiation
[255](https://docs.rs#255)                let h = 1e-5;
[256](https://docs.rs#256)                (polygamma(n - 1, x + h) - polygamma(n - 1, x - h)) / (2.0 * h)
[257](https://docs.rs#257)            }
[258](https://docs.rs#258)        }
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    }
[260](https://docs.rs#260)
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    /// Compute the beta function `B(a, b)`.
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    ///
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    /// # Algoritmo
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    ///
[265](https://docs.rs#265)    /// ```text
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    /// B(a, b) = \frac{\Gamma(a)\Gamma(b)}{\Gamma(a+b)}
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    /// ```
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    /// Computed efficiently via log-gamma to avoid overflow: `\exp(\ln\Gamma(a) + \ln\Gamma(b) - \ln\Gamma(a+b))`.
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    ///
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    /// # Referencias
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    ///
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §5.12.
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    pub fn beta(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
[275](https://docs.rs#275)        (lgamma(a) + lgamma(b) - lgamma(a + b)).exp()
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    }
[277](https://docs.rs#277)
[278](https://docs.rs#278)    /// Compute the logarithm of the beta function, `\ln(B(a, b))`.
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    ///
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    /// # Algoritmo
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    ///
[282](https://docs.rs#282)    /// ```text
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    /// \ln B(a, b) = \ln\Gamma(a) + \ln\Gamma(b) - \ln\Gamma(a+b)
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    /// ```
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    ///
[286](https://docs.rs#286)    /// # Referencias
[287](https://docs.rs#287)    ///
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §5.12.
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    pub fn betaln(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
[291](https://docs.rs#291)        lgamma(a) + lgamma(b) - lgamma(a + b)
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    }
[293](https://docs.rs#293)
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    /// Compute the regularized incomplete beta function `I_x(a, b)`.
[295](https://docs.rs#295)    ///
[296](https://docs.rs#296)    /// # Algoritmo
[297](https://docs.rs#297)    ///
[298](https://docs.rs#298)    /// ```text
[299](https://docs.rs#299)    /// I_x(a, b) = \frac{1}{B(a, b)} \int_0^x t^{a-1} (1-t)^{b-1} dt
[300](https://docs.rs#300)    /// ```
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    /// Uses a continued fraction expansion with Lentz's method. Symmetry `I_x(a,b) = 1 - I_{1-x}(b,a)`
[302](https://docs.rs#302)    /// is applied to ensure rapid convergence.
[303](https://docs.rs#303)    ///
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    /// # Precisión numérica
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    ///
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    /// Converges typically in less than 100 iterations. Tiny values `1e-30` used to prevent division by zero in Lentz's method.
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    ///
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    /// # Referencias
[309](https://docs.rs#309)    ///
[310](https://docs.rs#310)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §8.17.
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    /// - Abramowitz, M., & Stegun, I. A. (1964). *Handbook of Mathematical Functions*. Eq 26.5.8.
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    /// - Press, W. H., et al. (2007). *Numerical Recipes*. §6.4.
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    pub fn betainc(a: f64, b: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[315](https://docs.rs#315)        if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&x) {
[316](https://docs.rs#316)            return f64::NAN;
[317](https://docs.rs#317)        }
[318](https://docs.rs#318)        if x == 0.0 {
[319](https://docs.rs#319)            return 0.0;
[320](https://docs.rs#320)        }
[321](https://docs.rs#321)        if x == 1.0 {
[322](https://docs.rs#322)            return 1.0;
[323](https://docs.rs#323)        }
[324](https://docs.rs#324)
[325](https://docs.rs#325)        // Use continued fraction expansion
[326](https://docs.rs#326)        let bt = if x == 0.0 || x == 1.0 {
[327](https://docs.rs#327)            0.0
[328](https://docs.rs#328)        } else {
[329](https://docs.rs#329)            (lgamma(a + b) - lgamma(a) - lgamma(b) + a * x.ln() + b * (1.0 - x).ln()).exp()
[330](https://docs.rs#330)        };
[331](https://docs.rs#331)
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        // Symmetry relation
[333](https://docs.rs#333)        if x < (a + 1.0) / (a + b + 2.0) {
[334](https://docs.rs#334)            bt * betacf(a, b, x) / a
[335](https://docs.rs#335)        } else {
[336](https://docs.rs#336)            1.0 - bt * betacf(b, a, 1.0 - x) / b
[337](https://docs.rs#337)        }
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    }
[339](https://docs.rs#339)
[340](https://docs.rs#340)    // Continued fraction for beta function
[341](https://docs.rs#341)    fn betacf(a: f64, b: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[342](https://docs.rs#342)        let qab = a + b;
[343](https://docs.rs#343)        let qap = a + 1.0;
[344](https://docs.rs#344)        let qam = a - 1.0;
[345](https://docs.rs#345)        let mut c = 1.0;
[346](https://docs.rs#346)        let mut d = 1.0 - qab * x / qap;
[347](https://docs.rs#347)
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        if d.abs() < 1e-30 {
[349](https://docs.rs#349)            d = 1e-30;
[350](https://docs.rs#350)        }
[351](https://docs.rs#351)        d = 1.0 / d;
[352](https://docs.rs#352)        let mut h = d;
[353](https://docs.rs#353)
[354](https://docs.rs#354)        for m in 1..=100 {
[355](https://docs.rs#355)            let m_f = m as f64;
[356](https://docs.rs#356)            let m2 = 2.0 * m_f;
[357](https://docs.rs#357)
[358](https://docs.rs#358)            let aa = m_f * (b - m_f) * x / ((qam + m2) * (a + m2));
[359](https://docs.rs#359)            d = 1.0 + aa * d;
[360](https://docs.rs#360)            if d.abs() < 1e-30 {
[361](https://docs.rs#361)                d = 1e-30;
[362](https://docs.rs#362)            }
[363](https://docs.rs#363)            c = 1.0 + aa / c;
[364](https://docs.rs#364)            if c.abs() < 1e-30 {
[365](https://docs.rs#365)                c = 1e-30;
[366](https://docs.rs#366)            }
[367](https://docs.rs#367)            d = 1.0 / d;
[368](https://docs.rs#368)            h *= d * c;
[369](https://docs.rs#369)
[370](https://docs.rs#370)            let aa = -(a + m_f) * (qab + m_f) * x / ((a + m2) * (qap + m2));
[371](https://docs.rs#371)            d = 1.0 + aa * d;
[372](https://docs.rs#372)            if d.abs() < 1e-30 {
[373](https://docs.rs#373)                d = 1e-30;
[374](https://docs.rs#374)            }
[375](https://docs.rs#375)            c = 1.0 + aa / c;
[376](https://docs.rs#376)            if c.abs() < 1e-30 {
[377](https://docs.rs#377)                c = 1e-30;
[378](https://docs.rs#378)            }
[379](https://docs.rs#379)            d = 1.0 / d;
[380](https://docs.rs#380)            let del = d * c;
[381](https://docs.rs#381)            h *= del;
[382](https://docs.rs#382)
[383](https://docs.rs#383)            if (del - 1.0).abs() < 1e-10 {
[384](https://docs.rs#384)                break;
[385](https://docs.rs#385)            }
[386](https://docs.rs#386)        }
[387](https://docs.rs#387)
[388](https://docs.rs#388)        h
[389](https://docs.rs#389)    }
[390](https://docs.rs#390)
[391](https://docs.rs#391)    /// Compute the lower regularized incomplete gamma function `P(a, x)`.
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    ///
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    /// # Algoritmo
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    ///
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    /// ```text
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    /// P(a, x) = \frac{1}{\Gamma(a)} \int_0^x t^{a-1} e^{-t} dt
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    /// ```
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    /// Uses series expansion for `x < a + 1` and continued fractions for `x \ge a + 1`.
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    ///
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// # Precisión numérica
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    ///
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    /// Maximum 100 iterations. Truncation tolerance `1e-10`.
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    ///
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    /// # Referencias
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    ///
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §8.2.
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    /// - Press, W. H., et al. (2007). *Numerical Recipes*. §6.2.
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    pub fn gammainc(a: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[410](https://docs.rs#410)        if x < 0.0 || a <= 0.0 {
[411](https://docs.rs#411)            return f64::NAN;
[412](https://docs.rs#412)        }
[413](https://docs.rs#413)        if x == 0.0 {
[414](https://docs.rs#414)            return 0.0;
[415](https://docs.rs#415)        }
[416](https://docs.rs#416)
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        // Regularized incomplete gamma
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        if x < a + 1.0 {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)            // Use series expansion
[420](https://docs.rs#420)            gammaincser(a, x)
[421](https://docs.rs#421)        } else {
[422](https://docs.rs#422)            // Use continued fraction
[423](https://docs.rs#423)            1.0 - gammainccc(a, x)
[424](https://docs.rs#424)        }
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    }
[426](https://docs.rs#426)
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    /// Compute the upper regularized incomplete gamma function `Q(a, x)`.
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    ///
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    /// # Algoritmo
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    ///
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    /// ```text
[432](https://docs.rs#432)    /// Q(a, x) = 1 - P(a, x) = \frac{1}{\Gamma(a)} \int_x^\infty t^{a-1} e^{-t} dt
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    /// ```
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    ///
[435](https://docs.rs#435)    /// # Referencias
[436](https://docs.rs#436)    ///
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §8.2.
[438](https://docs.rs#438)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    pub fn gammaincc(a: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[440](https://docs.rs#440)        1.0 - gammainc(a, x)
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    }
[442](https://docs.rs#442)
[443](https://docs.rs#443)    fn gammaincser(a: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[444](https://docs.rs#444)        let gln = lgamma(a);
[445](https://docs.rs#445)        let mut ap = a;
[446](https://docs.rs#446)        let mut sum = 1.0 / a;
[447](https://docs.rs#447)        let mut del = sum;
[448](https://docs.rs#448)
[449](https://docs.rs#449)        for _ in 0..100 {
[450](https://docs.rs#450)            ap += 1.0;
[451](https://docs.rs#451)            del *= x / ap;
[452](https://docs.rs#452)            sum += del;
[453](https://docs.rs#453)            if del.abs() < sum.abs() * 1e-10 {
[454](https://docs.rs#454)                break;
[455](https://docs.rs#455)            }
[456](https://docs.rs#456)        }
[457](https://docs.rs#457)
[458](https://docs.rs#458)        sum * (-x + a * x.ln() - gln).exp()
[459](https://docs.rs#459)    }
[460](https://docs.rs#460)
[461](https://docs.rs#461)    fn gammainccc(a: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[462](https://docs.rs#462)        let gln = lgamma(a);
[463](https://docs.rs#463)        let mut b = x + 1.0 - a;
[464](https://docs.rs#464)        let mut c = 1.0 / 1e-30;
[465](https://docs.rs#465)        let mut d = 1.0 / b;
[466](https://docs.rs#466)        let mut h = d;
[467](https://docs.rs#467)
[468](https://docs.rs#468)        for i in 1..=100 {
[469](https://docs.rs#469)            let an = -(i as f64) * (i as f64 - a);
[470](https://docs.rs#470)            b += 2.0;
[471](https://docs.rs#471)            d = an * d + b;
[472](https://docs.rs#472)            if d.abs() < 1e-30 {
[473](https://docs.rs#473)                d = 1e-30;
[474](https://docs.rs#474)            }
[475](https://docs.rs#475)            c = b + an / c;
[476](https://docs.rs#476)            if c.abs() < 1e-30 {
[477](https://docs.rs#477)                c = 1e-30;
[478](https://docs.rs#478)            }
[479](https://docs.rs#479)            d = 1.0 / d;
[480](https://docs.rs#480)            let del = d * c;
[481](https://docs.rs#481)            h *= del;
[482](https://docs.rs#482)            if (del - 1.0).abs() < 1e-10 {
[483](https://docs.rs#483)                break;
[484](https://docs.rs#484)            }
[485](https://docs.rs#485)        }
[486](https://docs.rs#486)
[487](https://docs.rs#487)        (-x + a * x.ln() - gln).exp() * h
[488](https://docs.rs#488)    }
[489](https://docs.rs#489)
[490](https://docs.rs#490)    /// Compute the factorial `n!`.
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    ///
[492](https://docs.rs#492)    /// # Algoritmo
[493](https://docs.rs#493)    ///
[494](https://docs.rs#494)    /// Exact table lookup for `n <= 20`. Uses `\Gamma(n + 1)` for `n > 20`.
[495](https://docs.rs#495)    ///
[496](https://docs.rs#496)    /// # Referencias
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    ///
[498](https://docs.rs#498)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §5.2.
[499](https://docs.rs#499)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[500](https://docs.rs#500)    pub fn factorial(n: u64) -> f64 {
[501](https://docs.rs#501)        if n <= 20 {
[502](https://docs.rs#502)            FACTORIAL_TABLE[n as usize]
[503](https://docs.rs#503)        } else {
[504](https://docs.rs#504)            gamma(n as f64 + 1.0)
[505](https://docs.rs#505)        }
[506](https://docs.rs#506)    }
[507](https://docs.rs#507)
[508](https://docs.rs#508)    /// Compute the double factorial `n!!`.
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    ///
[510](https://docs.rs#510)    /// # Algoritmo
[511](https://docs.rs#511)    ///
[512](https://docs.rs#512)    /// Uses exact formulation scaling via the Gamma function for even values and ratio of factorials for odd values.
[513](https://docs.rs#513)    ///
[514](https://docs.rs#514)    /// # Referencias
[515](https://docs.rs#515)    ///
[516](https://docs.rs#516)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §5.2.
[517](https://docs.rs#517)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    pub fn double_factorial(n: u64) -> f64 {
[519](https://docs.rs#519)        if n <= 1 {
[520](https://docs.rs#520)            1.0
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        } else if n.is_multiple_of(2) {
[522](https://docs.rs#522)            // Even: n!! = n * (n-2) * ... * 4 * 2
[523](https://docs.rs#523)            let k = n / 2;
[524](https://docs.rs#524)            (2.0_f64).powi(k as i32) * gamma(k as f64 + 1.0)
[525](https://docs.rs#525)        } else {
[526](https://docs.rs#526)            // Odd: n!! = n * (n-2) * ... * 3 * 1
[527](https://docs.rs#527)            factorial(n) / double_factorial(n - 1)
[528](https://docs.rs#528)        }
[529](https://docs.rs#529)    }
[530](https://docs.rs#530)
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    const FACTORIAL_TABLE: [f64; 21] = [
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        1.0,                   // 0!
[533](https://docs.rs#533)        1.0,                   // 1!
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        2.0,                   // 2!
[535](https://docs.rs#535)        6.0,                   // 3!
[536](https://docs.rs#536)        24.0,                  // 4!
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        120.0,                 // 5!
[538](https://docs.rs#538)        720.0,                 // 6!
[539](https://docs.rs#539)        5040.0,                // 7!
[540](https://docs.rs#540)        40320.0,               // 8!
[541](https://docs.rs#541)        362880.0,              // 9!
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        3628800.0,             // 10!
[543](https://docs.rs#543)        39916800.0,            // 11!
[544](https://docs.rs#544)        479001600.0,           // 12!
[545](https://docs.rs#545)        6227020800.0,          // 13!
[546](https://docs.rs#546)        87178291200.0,         // 14!
[547](https://docs.rs#547)        1307674368000.0,       // 15!
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        20922789888000.0,      // 16!
[549](https://docs.rs#549)        355687428096000.0,     // 17!
[550](https://docs.rs#550)        6402373705728000.0,    // 18!
[551](https://docs.rs#551)        121645100408832000.0,  // 19!
[552](https://docs.rs#552)        2432902008176640000.0, // 20!
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    ];
[554](https://docs.rs#554)
[555](https://docs.rs#555)    /// Compute the binomial coefficient `C(n, k)`.
[556](https://docs.rs#556)    ///
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    /// # Algoritmo
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    ///
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    /// ```text
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    /// \binom{n}{k} = \frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}
[561](https://docs.rs#561)    /// ```
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    /// Computed analytically using logarithmic gamma expressions for large arguments.
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    ///
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    /// # Referencias
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    ///
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §1.2.
[567](https://docs.rs#567)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    pub fn binom(n: u64, k: u64) -> f64 {
[569](https://docs.rs#569)        if k > n {
[570](https://docs.rs#570)            0.0
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        } else if k == 0 || k == n {
[572](https://docs.rs#572)            1.0
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        } else {
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            (lgamma(n as f64 + 1.0) - lgamma(k as f64 + 1.0) - lgamma((n - k) as f64 + 1.0)).exp()
[575](https://docs.rs#575)        }
[576](https://docs.rs#576)    }
[577](https://docs.rs#577)}

[583](https://docs.rs#583)/// Error function and related functions
[584](https://docs.rs#584)pub mod erf_funcs {
[585](https://docs.rs#585)
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    /// Compute the error function `erf(x)`.
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    ///
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    /// # Algoritmo
[589](https://docs.rs#589)    ///
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    /// ```text
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    /// \text{erf}(x) = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \int_0^x e^{-t^2} dt
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    /// ```
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    /// Delegates to `libm::erf`.
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    ///
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    /// # Referencias
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    ///
[597](https://docs.rs#597)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §7.2.
[598](https://docs.rs#598)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    pub fn erf(x: f64) -> f64 {
[600](https://docs.rs#600)        libm::erf(x)
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    }
[602](https://docs.rs#602)
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    /// Compute the complementary error function `erfc(x)`.
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    ///
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    /// # Algoritmo
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    ///
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    /// ```text
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    /// \text{erfc}(x) = 1 - \text{erf}(x) = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \int_x^\infty e^{-t^2} dt
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    /// ```
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    /// Delegates to `libm::erfc`. Numerically stable for large `x`.
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    ///
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    /// # Referencias
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    ///
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §7.2.
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    pub fn erfc(x: f64) -> f64 {
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        libm::erfc(x)
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    }
[619](https://docs.rs#619)
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    /// Compute the inverse error function `erfinv(y)`.
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    ///
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    /// # Algoritmo
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    ///
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    /// Returns `x` such that `erf(x) = y`.
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    /// Uses a rational Chebyshev approximation for evaluation.
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    ///
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    /// # Precisión numérica
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    ///
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    /// The polynomial coefficients are derived from rational Chebyshev approximations, achieving near machine precision.
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    ///
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    /// # Referencias
[632](https://docs.rs#632)    ///
[633](https://docs.rs#633)    /// - Cody, W. J. (1969). Rational Chebyshev Approximations for the Error Function.
[634](https://docs.rs#634)    ///   *Mathematics of Computation*, 23(107), 631-638. DOI: [10.1090/S0025-5718-1969-0240954-4](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-1969-0240954-4)
[635](https://docs.rs#635)    pub fn erfinv(y: f64) -> f64 {
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        if !(-1.0..=1.0).contains(&y) {
[637](https://docs.rs#637)            return f64::NAN;
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        }
[639](https://docs.rs#639)        if y == -1.0 {
[640](https://docs.rs#640)            return f64::NEG_INFINITY;
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        }
[642](https://docs.rs#642)        if y == 1.0 {
[643](https://docs.rs#643)            return f64::INFINITY;
[644](https://docs.rs#644)        }
[645](https://docs.rs#645)        if y == 0.0 {
[646](https://docs.rs#646)            return 0.0;
[647](https://docs.rs#647)        }
[648](https://docs.rs#648)
[649](https://docs.rs#649)        // Rational approximation
[650](https://docs.rs#650)        let a = y.abs();
[651](https://docs.rs#651)        let sign = y.signum();
[652](https://docs.rs#652)
[653](https://docs.rs#653)        if a <= 0.7 {
[654](https://docs.rs#654)            let x = a * a;
[655](https://docs.rs#655)            let r = a
[656](https://docs.rs#656)                * ((((-0.140543331 * x + 0.914624893) * x - 1.64536091) * x + 0.886226899)
[657](https://docs.rs#657)                    / ((((0.012229801 * x - 0.329097515) * x + 1.442710462) * x - 2.118377725)
[658](https://docs.rs#658)                        * x
[659](https://docs.rs#659)                        + 1.0));
[660](https://docs.rs#660)            return sign * r;
[661](https://docs.rs#661)        }
[662](https://docs.rs#662)
[663](https://docs.rs#663)        let x = (-((1.0 - a) / 2.0).ln()).sqrt();
[664](https://docs.rs#664)        let r = (((1.641345311 * x + 3.429567803) * x - 1.624906493) * x - 1.970840454)
[665](https://docs.rs#665)            / ((1.637067800 * x + 3.543889200) * x + 1.0);
[666](https://docs.rs#666)
[667](https://docs.rs#667)        sign * r
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    }
[669](https://docs.rs#669)
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    /// Compute the inverse complementary error function `erfcinv(y)`.
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    ///
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    /// # Algoritmo
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    ///
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    /// Evaluated simply as `erfinv(1 - y)`. Note that precision may degrade for values of `y` extremely close to 0.
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    ///
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    /// # Referencias
[677](https://docs.rs#677)    ///
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    /// - Cody, W. J. (1969). Rational Chebyshev Approximations for the Error Function.
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    ///   DOI: [10.1090/S0025-5718-1969-0240954-4](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-1969-0240954-4)
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    pub fn erfcinv(y: f64) -> f64 {
[681](https://docs.rs#681)        erfinv(1.0 - y)
[682](https://docs.rs#682)    }
[683](https://docs.rs#683)
[684](https://docs.rs#684)    /// Compute the scaled complementary error function `erfcx(x)`.
[685](https://docs.rs#685)    ///
[686](https://docs.rs#686)    /// # Algoritmo
[687](https://docs.rs#687)    ///
[688](https://docs.rs#688)    /// ```text
[689](https://docs.rs#689)    /// \text{erfcx}(x) = e^{x^2} \text{erfc}(x)
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    /// ```
[691](https://docs.rs#691)    ///
[692](https://docs.rs#692)    /// # Precisión numérica
[693](https://docs.rs#693)    ///
[694](https://docs.rs#694)    /// Uses an asymptotic expansion `1 / (x \sqrt{\pi})` for `x > 26.0` to avoid `NaN` caused by multiplying extremely large `e^{x^2}` with extremely small `erfc(x)`.
[695](https://docs.rs#695)    ///
[696](https://docs.rs#696)    /// # Referencias
[697](https://docs.rs#697)    ///
[698](https://docs.rs#698)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §7.2.
[699](https://docs.rs#699)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[700](https://docs.rs#700)    pub fn erfcx(x: f64) -> f64 {
[701](https://docs.rs#701)        // For large x, use asymptotic expansion
[702](https://docs.rs#702)        if x > 26.0 {
[703](https://docs.rs#703)            let inv_sqrtpi = 1.0 / std::f64::consts::PI.sqrt();
[704](https://docs.rs#704)            return inv_sqrtpi / x;
[705](https://docs.rs#705)        }
[706](https://docs.rs#706)
[707](https://docs.rs#707)        (x * x).exp() * erfc(x)
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    }
[709](https://docs.rs#709)
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    /// Compute the imaginary error function `erfi(x)`.
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    ///
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    /// # Algoritmo
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    ///
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    /// ```text
[715](https://docs.rs#715)    /// \text{erfi}(x) = -i \text{erf}(ix) = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \int_0^x e^{t^2} dt
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    /// ```
[717](https://docs.rs#717)    /// Evaluated using a Maclaurin series expansion.
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    ///
[719](https://docs.rs#719)    /// # Precisión numérica
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    ///
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    /// Uses a maximum of 100 series terms with a relative precision tolerance of `1e-15`.
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    /// May overflow for moderately large `x` since the function grows exponentially as `e^{x^2}/x`.
[723](https://docs.rs#723)    ///
[724](https://docs.rs#724)    /// # Referencias
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    ///
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §7.2.
[727](https://docs.rs#727)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[728](https://docs.rs#728)    pub fn erfi(x: f64) -> f64 {
[729](https://docs.rs#729)        // Series expansion
[730](https://docs.rs#730)        let two_sqrtpi = 2.0 / std::f64::consts::PI.sqrt();
[731](https://docs.rs#731)        let x2 = x * x;
[732](https://docs.rs#732)
[733](https://docs.rs#733)        let mut sum = x;
[734](https://docs.rs#734)        let mut term = x;
[735](https://docs.rs#735)
[736](https://docs.rs#736)        for n in 1..100 {
[737](https://docs.rs#737)            term *= x2 / n as f64;
[738](https://docs.rs#738)            let new_term = term / (2 * n + 1) as f64;
[739](https://docs.rs#739)            sum += new_term;
[740](https://docs.rs#740)            if new_term.abs() < sum.abs() * 1e-15 {
[741](https://docs.rs#741)                break;
[742](https://docs.rs#742)            }
[743](https://docs.rs#743)        }
[744](https://docs.rs#744)
[745](https://docs.rs#745)        two_sqrtpi * sum
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    }
[747](https://docs.rs#747)
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    /// Compute the Dawson function `F(x)`.
[749](https://docs.rs#749)    ///
[750](https://docs.rs#750)    /// # Algoritmo
[751](https://docs.rs#751)    ///
[752](https://docs.rs#752)    /// ```text
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    /// F(x) = e^{-x^2} \int_0^x e^{t^2} dt
[754](https://docs.rs#754)    /// ```
[755](https://docs.rs#755)    /// Uses a Taylor series for `|x| < 1` and an asymptotic relation to `erfi(x)` for larger magnitudes.
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    ///
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    /// # Referencias
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    ///
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §7.2.
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    pub fn dawsn(x: f64) -> f64 {
[762](https://docs.rs#762)        let x2 = x * x;
[763](https://docs.rs#763)
[764](https://docs.rs#764)        // For small x, use Taylor series
[765](https://docs.rs#765)        if x.abs() < 1.0 {
[766](https://docs.rs#766)            let mut sum = x;
[767](https://docs.rs#767)            let mut term = x;
[768](https://docs.rs#768)
[769](https://docs.rs#769)            for n in 1..50 {
[770](https://docs.rs#770)                term *= -2.0 * x2 / (2 * n + 1) as f64;
[771](https://docs.rs#771)                sum += term;
[772](https://docs.rs#772)                if term.abs() < sum.abs() * 1e-15 {
[773](https://docs.rs#773)                    break;
[774](https://docs.rs#774)                }
[775](https://docs.rs#775)            }
[776](https://docs.rs#776)
[777](https://docs.rs#777)            return sum;
[778](https://docs.rs#778)        }
[779](https://docs.rs#779)
[780](https://docs.rs#780)        // For large x, use asymptotic expansion
[781](https://docs.rs#781)        0.5 * std::f64::consts::PI.sqrt() * (-x2).exp() * erfi(x)
[782](https://docs.rs#782)    }
[783](https://docs.rs#783)
[784](https://docs.rs#784)    /// Compute the standard Normal cumulative distribution function (CDF).
[785](https://docs.rs#785)    ///
[786](https://docs.rs#786)    /// # Algoritmo
[787](https://docs.rs#787)    ///
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    /// ```text
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    /// \Phi(x) = \frac{1}{2} \text{erfc}\left(\frac{-x}{\sqrt{2}}\right)
[790](https://docs.rs#790)    /// ```
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    ///
[792](https://docs.rs#792)    /// # Referencias
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    ///
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions.
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    pub fn ndtr(x: f64) -> f64 {
[797](https://docs.rs#797)        0.5 * erfc(-x / std::f64::consts::SQRT_2)
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    }
[799](https://docs.rs#799)
[800](https://docs.rs#800)    /// Compute the inverse standard Normal cumulative distribution function (PPF).
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    ///
[802](https://docs.rs#802)    /// # Algoritmo
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    ///
[804](https://docs.rs#804)    /// ```text
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    /// \Phi^{-1}(p) = -\sqrt{2} \text{erfcinv}(2p)
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    /// ```
[807](https://docs.rs#807)    ///
[808](https://docs.rs#808)    /// # Referencias
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    ///
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions.
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    pub fn ndtri(p: f64) -> f64 {
[813](https://docs.rs#813)        -std::f64::consts::SQRT_2 * erfcinv(2.0 * p)
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    }
[815](https://docs.rs#815)}

[825](https://docs.rs#825)    /// Compute the Bessel function of the first kind, order 0, `J_0(x)`.

[853](https://docs.rs#853)    /// Compute the Bessel function of the first kind, integer order `n`, `J_n(x)`.
[854](https://docs.rs#854)    ///
[855](https://docs.rs#855)    /// # Algoritmo
[856](https://docs.rs#856)    ///
[857](https://docs.rs#857)    /// Delegates to `libm::jn`.
[858](https://docs.rs#858)    ///
[859](https://docs.rs#859)    /// # Referencias
[860](https://docs.rs#860)    ///
[861](https://docs.rs#861)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.2.

[866](https://docs.rs#866)
[867](https://docs.rs#867)    /// Compute the Bessel function of the first kind, real order `\nu`, `J_\nu(x)`.
[868](https://docs.rs#868)    ///
[869](https://docs.rs#869)    /// # Algoritmo
[870](https://docs.rs#870)    ///
[871](https://docs.rs#871)    /// If `\nu` is integer, delegates to `jn`. Otherwise, computes via a Maclaurin series expansion.
[872](https://docs.rs#872)    ///
[873](https://docs.rs#873)    /// # Precisión numérica
[874](https://docs.rs#874)    ///
[875](https://docs.rs#875)    /// The series expansion converges well for small to moderate `x`. It evaluates up to 100 terms until relative correction drops below `1e-15`.
[876](https://docs.rs#876)    ///
[877](https://docs.rs#877)    /// # Referencias
[878](https://docs.rs#878)    ///
[879](https://docs.rs#879)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.2.
[880](https://docs.rs#880)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[881](https://docs.rs#881)    pub fn jv(v: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[882](https://docs.rs#882)        if v.floor() == v {
[883](https://docs.rs#883)            jn(v as i32, x)
[884](https://docs.rs#884)        } else {
[885](https://docs.rs#885)            // Use series expansion for fractional order
[886](https://docs.rs#886)            jv_series(v, x)
[887](https://docs.rs#887)        }
[888](https://docs.rs#888)    }
[889](https://docs.rs#889)
[890](https://docs.rs#890)    fn jv_series(v: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[891](https://docs.rs#891)        let x2 = x / 2.0;
[892](https://docs.rs#892)        let mut sum = 0.0;
[893](https://docs.rs#893)        let mut term = x2.powf(v) / gamma_funcs::gamma(v + 1.0);
[894](https://docs.rs#894)
[895](https://docs.rs#895)        for k in 0..100 {
[896](https://docs.rs#896)            sum += term;
[897](https://docs.rs#897)            term *= -x2 * x2 / ((k + 1) as f64 * (v + k as f64 + 1.0));
[898](https://docs.rs#898)            if term.abs() < sum.abs() * 1e-15 {
[899](https://docs.rs#899)                break;
[900](https://docs.rs#900)            }
[901](https://docs.rs#901)        }
[902](https://docs.rs#902)
[903](https://docs.rs#903)        sum
[904](https://docs.rs#904)    }
[905](https://docs.rs#905)

[934](https://docs.rs#934)    /// Compute the Bessel function of the second kind, integer order `n`, `Y_n(x)`.
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    ///
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    /// # Algoritmo
[937](https://docs.rs#937)    ///
[938](https://docs.rs#938)    /// Delegates to `libm::yn`.
[939](https://docs.rs#939)    ///
[940](https://docs.rs#940)    /// # Referencias
[941](https://docs.rs#941)    ///
[942](https://docs.rs#942)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.2.
[943](https://docs.rs#943)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[944](https://docs.rs#944)    pub fn yn(n: i32, x: f64) -> f64 {
[945](https://docs.rs#945)        libm::yn(n, x)
[946](https://docs.rs#946)    }
[947](https://docs.rs#947)
[948](https://docs.rs#948)    /// Compute the Bessel function of the second kind, real order `\nu`, `Y_\nu(x)`.
[949](https://docs.rs#949)    ///
[950](https://docs.rs#950)    /// # Algoritmo
[951](https://docs.rs#951)    ///
[952](https://docs.rs#952)    /// Evaluated using the standard identity:
[953](https://docs.rs#953)    /// ```text
[954](https://docs.rs#954)    /// Y_\nu(x) = \frac{J_\nu(x) \cos(\nu\pi) - J_{-\nu}(x)}{\sin(\nu\pi)}
[955](https://docs.rs#955)    /// ```
[956](https://docs.rs#956)    ///
[957](https://docs.rs#957)    /// # Precisión numérica
[958](https://docs.rs#958)    ///
[959](https://docs.rs#959)    /// Suffers from catastrophic cancellation if `\nu` is close to an integer. However, the logic handles exact integers explicitly.
[960](https://docs.rs#960)    ///
[961](https://docs.rs#961)    /// # Referencias
[962](https://docs.rs#962)    ///
[963](https://docs.rs#963)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.2.
[964](https://docs.rs#964)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[965](https://docs.rs#965)    pub fn yv(v: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[966](https://docs.rs#966)        if v.floor() == v {
[967](https://docs.rs#967)            yn(v as i32, x)
[968](https://docs.rs#968)        } else {
[969](https://docs.rs#969)            // Yv = (Jv cos(v*pi) - J-v) / sin(v*pi)
[970](https://docs.rs#970)            let vpi = v * std::f64::consts::PI;
[971](https://docs.rs#971)            (jv(v, x) * vpi.cos() - jv(-v, x)) / vpi.sin()
[972](https://docs.rs#972)        }
[973](https://docs.rs#973)    }
[974](https://docs.rs#974)
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    /// Compute the modified Bessel function of the first kind, order 0, `I_0(x)`.
[976](https://docs.rs#976)    ///
[977](https://docs.rs#977)    /// # Algoritmo
[978](https://docs.rs#978)    ///
[979](https://docs.rs#979)    /// Evaluated using piecewise polynomial approximations divided at `|x| = 3.75`.
[980](https://docs.rs#980)    ///
[981](https://docs.rs#981)    /// # Precisión numérica
[982](https://docs.rs#982)    ///
[983](https://docs.rs#983)    /// The polynomial coefficients are standard minimax approximations yielding precision up to `1e-7` to `1e-8`.
[984](https://docs.rs#984)    /// See Abramowitz & Stegun Eq. 9.8.1 and 9.8.2.
[985](https://docs.rs#985)    ///
[986](https://docs.rs#986)    /// # Referencias
[987](https://docs.rs#987)    ///
[988](https://docs.rs#988)    /// - Abramowitz, M., & Stegun, I. A. (1964). *Handbook of Mathematical Functions*. Eqs. 9.8.1 - 9.8.2.
[989](https://docs.rs#989)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.25.
[990](https://docs.rs#990)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[991](https://docs.rs#991)    pub fn i0(x: f64) -> f64 {
[992](https://docs.rs#992)        let ax = x.abs();
[993](https://docs.rs#993)
[994](https://docs.rs#994)        if ax < 3.75 {
[995](https://docs.rs#995)            let y = (x / 3.75).powi(2);
[996](https://docs.rs#996)            1.0 + y
[997](https://docs.rs#997)                * (3.5156229
[998](https://docs.rs#998)                    + y * (3.0899424
[999](https://docs.rs#999)                        + y * (1.2067492 + y * (0.2659732 + y * (0.0360768 + y * 0.0045813)))))
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)        } else {
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)            let y = 3.75 / ax;
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)            (ax.exp() / ax.sqrt())
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)                * (0.39894228
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)                    + y * (0.01328592
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)                        + y * (0.00225319
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)                            + y * (-0.00157565
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)                                + y * (0.00916281
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)                                    + y * (-0.02057706
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)                                        + y * (0.02635537
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)                                            + y * (-0.01647633 + y * 0.00392377))))))))
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)        }
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)    }
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)    /// Compute the modified Bessel function of the first kind, order 1, `I_1(x)`.
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)    ///
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)    /// # Algoritmo
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)    ///
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)    /// Evaluated using piecewise polynomial approximations divided at `|x| = 3.75`.
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)    ///
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)    /// # Precisión numérica
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)    ///
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)    /// The polynomial coefficients are from Abramowitz & Stegun Eq. 9.8.3 and 9.8.4.
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)    ///
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)    /// # Referencias
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)    ///
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)    /// - Abramowitz, M., & Stegun, I. A. (1964). *Handbook of Mathematical Functions*. Eqs. 9.8.3 - 9.8.4.
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.25.
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)    pub fn i1(x: f64) -> f64 {
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)        let ax = x.abs();
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)        let result = if ax < 3.75 {
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)            let y = (x / 3.75).powi(2);
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)            ax * (0.5
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)                + y * (0.87890594
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)                    + y * (0.51498869
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)                        + y * (0.15084934 + y * (0.02658733 + y * (0.00301532 + y * 0.00032411))))))
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)        } else {
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)            let y = 3.75 / ax;
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)            (ax.exp() / ax.sqrt())
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)                * (0.39894228
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)                    + y * (-0.03988024
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)                        + y * (-0.00362018
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)                            + y * (0.00163801
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)                                + y * (-0.01031555
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)                                    + y * (0.02282967
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)                                        + y * (-0.02895312
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)                                            + y * (0.01787654 + y * (-0.00420059)))))))))
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)        };
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)        if x < 0.0 {
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)            -result
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)        } else {
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)            result
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)        }
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)    }
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)    /// Compute the modified Bessel function of the first kind, real order `\nu`, `I_\nu(x)`.
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)    ///
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)    /// # Algoritmo
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)    ///
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)    /// Evaluated using a series expansion for non-integer configurations.
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)    ///
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)    /// # Precisión numérica
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)    ///
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)    /// Evaluates up to 100 terms in the power series, stopping when relative contribution is `< 1e-15`.
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)    ///
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)    /// # Referencias
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)    ///
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.25.
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)    pub fn iv(v: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)        if v == 0.0 {
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)            i0(x)
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)        } else if v == 1.0 {
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)            i1(x)
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)        } else {
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)            // Series expansion
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)            let x2 = x / 2.0;
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)            let mut sum = 0.0;
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)            let mut term = x2.powf(v) / gamma_funcs::gamma(v + 1.0);
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)            for k in 0..100 {
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)                sum += term;
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)                term *= x2 * x2 / ((k + 1) as f64 * (v + k as f64 + 1.0));
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)                if term.abs() < sum.abs() * 1e-15 {
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)                    break;
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)                }
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)            }
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)            sum
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)        }
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)    }
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)    /// Compute the modified Bessel function of the second kind, order 0, `K_0(x)`.
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)    ///
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)    /// # Algoritmo
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)    ///
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)    /// Computed using polynomial approximations split at `x = 2.0`.
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)    ///
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)    /// # Precisión numérica
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)    ///
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)    /// Employs standard minimax polynomials. Coefficients correspond to Abramowitz & Stegun Eq. 9.8.5 and 9.8.6.
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)    ///
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)    /// # Referencias
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)    ///
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)    /// - Abramowitz, M., & Stegun, I. A. (1964). *Handbook of Mathematical Functions*. Eqs. 9.8.5 - 9.8.6.
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.25.
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)    pub fn k0(x: f64) -> f64 {
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)        if x <= 2.0 {
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)            let y = x * x / 4.0;
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)            (-x.ln() / 2.0 + 0.57721566) * i0(x)
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)                + (-0.57721566
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)                    + y * (0.42278420
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)                        + y * (0.23069756
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)                            + y * (0.03488590
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)                                + y * (0.00262698 + y * (0.00010750 + y * 0.00000740))))))
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)        } else {
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)            let y = 2.0 / x;
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)            ((-x).exp() / x.sqrt())
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)                * (1.25331414
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)                    + y * (-0.07832358
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)                        + y * (0.02189568
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)                            + y * (-0.01062446
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)                                + y * (0.00587872 + y * (-0.00251540 + y * 0.00053208))))))
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)        }
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)    }
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)    /// Compute the modified Bessel function of the second kind, order 1, `K_1(x)`.
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)    ///
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)    /// # Algoritmo
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)    ///
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)    /// Computed using polynomial approximations split at `x = 2.0`.
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)    ///
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)    /// # Precisión numérica
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)    ///
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)    /// Employs standard minimax polynomials. Coefficients correspond to Abramowitz & Stegun Eq. 9.8.7 and 9.8.8.
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)    ///
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)    /// # Referencias
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)    ///
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)    /// - Abramowitz, M., & Stegun, I. A. (1964). *Handbook of Mathematical Functions*. Eqs. 9.8.7 - 9.8.8.
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.25.
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)    pub fn k1(x: f64) -> f64 {
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)        if x <= 2.0 {
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)            let y = x * x / 4.0;
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)            (x.ln() / 2.0) * i1(x)
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)                + (1.0 / x)
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)                    * (1.0
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)                        + y * (0.15443144
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)                            + y * (-0.67278579
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)                                + y * (-0.18156897
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)                                    + y * (-0.01919402 + y * (-0.00110404 + y * (-0.00004686)))))))
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)        } else {
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)            let y = 2.0 / x;
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)            ((-x).exp() / x.sqrt())
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)                * (1.25331414
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)                    + y * (0.23498619
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)                        + y * (-0.03655620
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)                            + y * (0.01504268
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)                                + y * (-0.00780353 + y * (0.00325614 + y * (-0.00068245)))))))
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)        }
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)    }
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)    /// Compute the modified Bessel function of the second kind, real order `\nu`, `K_\nu(x)`.
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)    ///
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)    /// # Algoritmo
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)    ///
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)    /// Utilizes standard forward recurrence leveraging `K_0` and `K_1` when generating higher order responses.
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)    ///
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)    /// # Referencias
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)    ///
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.25.
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)    pub fn kv(v: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)        if v == 0.0 {
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)            k0(x)
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)        } else if v == 1.0 {
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)            k1(x)
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)        } else {
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)            // Use recurrence relation
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)            let mut k_prev = k0(x);
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)            let mut k_curr = k1(x);
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)            for n in 1..(v.abs() as i32) {
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)                let k_next = k_prev + (2.0 * n as f64 / x) * k_curr;
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)                k_prev = k_curr;
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)                k_curr = k_next;
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)            }
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)            k_curr
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)        }
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)    }
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)    /// Compute the spherical Bessel function of the first kind, `j_n(x)`.
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)    ///
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)    /// # Algoritmo
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)    ///
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)    /// ```text
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)    /// j_n(x) = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2x}} J_{n+1/2}(x)
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)    /// ```
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)    ///
[1204](https://docs.rs#1204)    /// # Referencias
[1205](https://docs.rs#1205)    ///
[1206](https://docs.rs#1206)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.47.
[1207](https://docs.rs#1207)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1208](https://docs.rs#1208)    pub fn spherical_jn(n: usize, x: f64) -> f64 {
[1209](https://docs.rs#1209)        if x == 0.0 {
[1210](https://docs.rs#1210)            return if n == 0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 };
[1211](https://docs.rs#1211)        }
[1212](https://docs.rs#1212)
[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)        // j_n(x) = sqrt(pi / (2x)) * J_{n+1/2}(x)
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)        let factor = (std::f64::consts::PI / (2.0 * x)).sqrt();
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)        factor * jv(n as f64 + 0.5, x)
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)    }
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)    /// Compute the spherical Bessel function of the second kind, `y_n(x)`.
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)    ///
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)    /// # Algoritmo
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)    ///
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)    /// ```text
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)    /// y_n(x) = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2x}} Y_{n+1/2}(x)
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)    /// ```
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)    ///
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)    /// # Referencias
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)    ///
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §10.47.
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)    pub fn spherical_yn(n: usize, x: f64) -> f64 {
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)        // y_n(x) = sqrt(pi / (2x)) * Y_{n+1/2}(x)
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)        let factor = (std::f64::consts::PI / (2.0 * x)).sqrt();
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)        factor * yv(n as f64 + 0.5, x)
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)    }

[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)/// Airy functions Ai(x), Bi(x) and their derivatives.
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)///
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)/// # References
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)/// - NIST DLMF §9: <https://dlmf.nist.gov/9>
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)/// - Abramowitz & Stegun, Chapter 10
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)pub mod airy {
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)    use std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_4;
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)    // Ai(0) = 3^{-2/3}/Γ(2/3), −Ai'(0) = 3^{-1/3}/Γ(1/3) — NIST DLMF 9.2.3
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)    const AI0: f64 = 0.355_028_053_887_817_2;
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)    const C2: f64 = 0.25881940379280679;
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)    const SQRT3: f64 = 1.732_050_807_568_877_2_f64;
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)    const SQRTPI: f64 = 1.7724538509055159_f64;
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)    // Taylor power series — NIST DLMF 9.2.2, A&S 10.4.3–10.4.4
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)    // f = Σ a_k, a_0=1, a_{k+1} = a_k·x³/((3k+2)(3k+3))
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)    // g = Σ b_k, b_0=x,  b_{k+1} = b_k·x³/((3k+3)(3k+4))
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)    // f'(x) = (1/x)·Σ_{k≥0}(3k+3)·a_{k+1},  g'(x) = 1 + (1/x)·Σ_{k≥0}(3k+4)·b_{k+1}
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)    fn taylor(x: f64) -> (f64, f64, f64, f64) {
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)        let x3 = x * x * x;
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)        let (mut f, mut g) = (1.0_f64, x);
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)        let (mut fp_num, mut gp_num) = (0.0_f64, 0.0_f64);
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)        let (mut ak, mut bk) = (1.0_f64, x);
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)        for k in 0_usize..60 {
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)            let kf = k as f64;
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)            let ak1 = ak * x3 / ((3.0 * kf + 2.0) * (3.0 * kf + 3.0));
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)            let bk1 = bk * x3 / ((3.0 * kf + 3.0) * (3.0 * kf + 4.0));
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)            f += ak1;
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)            g += bk1;
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)            fp_num += (3.0 * kf + 3.0) * ak1;
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)            gp_num += (3.0 * kf + 4.0) * bk1;
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)            if ak1.abs() < 1e-16 * (f.abs() + 1e-30) && bk1.abs() < 1e-16 * (g.abs() + 1e-30) {
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)                break;
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)            }
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)            ak = ak1;
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)            bk = bk1;
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)        }
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)        let (fp, gp) = if x.abs() > 1e-30 {
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)            (fp_num / x, 1.0 + gp_num / x)
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)        } else {
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)            (0.0, 1.0)
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)        };
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)        (f, fp, g, gp)
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)    }
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)    // Olver u_s, v_s coefficients — NIST DLMF 9.7.1
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)    // u_0=1, u_s = u_{s-1}·(6s−5)(6s−3)(6s−1)/(216s)
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)    // v_0=1, v_s = −(6s+1)/(6s−1)·u_s  for s≥1
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)    fn olver() -> ([f64; 13], [f64; 13]) {
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)        let mut u = [0.0_f64; 13];
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)        let mut v = [0.0_f64; 13];
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)        u[0] = 1.0;
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)        v[0] = 1.0;
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)        for s in 1_usize..=12 {
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)            let sf = s as f64;
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)            u[s] = u[s - 1] * (6.0 * sf - 5.0) * (6.0 * sf - 3.0) * (6.0 * sf - 1.0) / (216.0 * sf);
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)            v[s] = -(6.0 * sf + 1.0) / (6.0 * sf - 1.0) * u[s];
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)        }
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)        (u, v)
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)    }
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)    // Asymptotic series for x > 5 — NIST DLMF 9.7.5, 9.7.6, 9.7.9, 9.7.10
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)    // Returns (ua, va, un, vn):
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)    //   ua = Σ_s (−1)^s u_s/ζ^s,  va = Σ_s (−1)^s v_s/ζ^s  (alternating, for Ai/Ai')
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)    //   un = Σ_s u_s/ζ^s,          vn = Σ_s v_s/ζ^s          (for Bi/Bi')
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)    // Truncated at the smallest term (optimal asymptotic truncation).
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)    fn asym_pos(zeta: f64) -> (f64, f64, f64, f64) {
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)        let (u, v) = olver();
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)        let (mut ua, mut va, mut un, mut vn) = (1.0_f64, 1.0_f64, 1.0_f64, 1.0_f64);
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)        let mut zp = zeta;
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)        let mut prev = 1.0_f64;
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)        for s in 1_usize..=12 {
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)            let tu = u[s] / zp;
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)            if tu > prev {
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)                break; // optimal truncation: stop at divergence
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)            }
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)            let sign = if s % 2 == 0 { 1.0_f64 } else { -1.0_f64 };
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)            ua += sign * u[s] / zp;
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)            va += sign * v[s] / zp;
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)            un += u[s] / zp;
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)            vn += v[s] / zp;
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)            prev = tu;
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)            zp *= zeta;
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)        }
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)        (ua, va, un, vn)
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)    }
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)    // Oscillatory asymptotic for x < −5 — NIST DLMF 9.7.7, 9.7.11
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)    // With z = −x > 0, ζ = (2/3)z^{3/2}, θ = ζ + π/4, returns (fe, fo, ge, go):
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)    //   fe = Σ_s (−1)^s u_{2s}/ζ^{2s},   fo = Σ_s (−1)^s u_{2s+1}/ζ^{2s+1}
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)    //   ge = Σ_s (−1)^s v_{2s}/ζ^{2s},   go = Σ_s (−1)^s v_{2s+1}/ζ^{2s+1}
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)    // Even and odd subseries are truncated independently at their smallest term.
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333)    fn asym_neg(zeta: f64) -> (f64, f64, f64, f64) {
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)        let (u, v) = olver();
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)        let z2 = zeta * zeta;
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)        // Even subseries: optimal truncation when term grows
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)        let (mut fe, mut ge) = (1.0_f64, 1.0_f64);
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)        let mut z2s = z2;
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)        let mut prev_e = 1.0_f64;
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)        for s in 1_usize..=5 {
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)            let te = u[2 * s] / z2s;
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)            if te > prev_e {
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)                break;
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)            }
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)            let sign = if s % 2 == 0 { 1.0_f64 } else { -1.0_f64 };
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)            fe += sign * u[2 * s] / z2s;
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)            ge += sign * v[2 * s] / z2s;
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)            prev_e = te;
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)            z2s *= z2;
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)        }
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)        // Odd subseries: optimal truncation when term grows
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)        let (mut fo, mut go) = (u[1] / zeta, v[1] / zeta);
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)        let mut z2s1 = zeta * z2;
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)        let mut prev_o = u[1] / zeta;
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)        for s in 1_usize..=5 {
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)            let to_val = u[2 * s + 1] / z2s1;
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)            if to_val > prev_o {
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)                break;
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)            }
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)            let sign = if s % 2 == 0 { 1.0_f64 } else { -1.0_f64 };
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)            fo += sign * u[2 * s + 1] / z2s1;
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)            go += sign * v[2 * s + 1] / z2s1;
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)            prev_o = to_val;
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)            z2s1 *= z2;
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)        }
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)        (fe, fo, ge, go)
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)    }
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)    /// Compute the Airy function `Ai(x)` and its derivative `Ai'(x)`.
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)    ///
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)    /// # Algorithm
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)    /// - `|x| ≤ 5`: Taylor power series (NIST DLMF 9.2.2, A&S 10.4.3–10.4.4)
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)    /// - `x > 5`: Olver asymptotic expansion (NIST DLMF 9.7.5–9.7.6)
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)    /// - `x < −5`: Oscillatory asymptotic (NIST DLMF 9.7.7, 9.7.11)
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)    pub fn airy_ai(x: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)        if x.abs() <= 5.0 {
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)            let (f, fp, g, gp) = taylor(x);
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)            (AI0 * f - C2 * g, AI0 * fp - C2 * gp)
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)        } else if x > 5.0 {
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)            // ζ = (2/3)x^{3/2}; Ai ~ e^{−ζ}/(2√π x^{1/4})·Σ(−1)^s u_s/ζ^s
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)            let zeta = 2.0 / 3.0 * x.powf(1.5);
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)            let x14 = x.powf(0.25);
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)            let en = (-zeta).exp();
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)            let (ua, va, _, _) = asym_pos(zeta);
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)            (
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)                en * ua / (2.0 * SQRTPI * x14),
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)                -en * x14 * va / (2.0 * SQRTPI),
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)            )
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)        } else {
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)            // θ = ζ + π/4; Ai(−z) = z^{−1/4}/√π·(sin θ·fe + cos θ·fo)
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)            // Ai'(−z) = z^{1/4}/√π·(−cos θ·ge + sin θ·go)
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)            let t = -x;
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)            let zeta = 2.0 / 3.0 * t.powf(1.5);
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)            let t14 = t.powf(0.25);
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)            let th = zeta + FRAC_PI_4;
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)            let (s, c) = (th.sin(), th.cos());
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)            let (fe, fo, ge, go) = asym_neg(zeta);
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)            let ai = (s * fe + c * fo) / (SQRTPI * t14);
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)            let aip = t14 / SQRTPI * (-c * ge + s * go);
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)            (ai, aip)
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)        }
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)    }
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)    /// Compute the Airy function `Bi(x)` and its derivative `Bi'(x)`.
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)    ///
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)    /// # Algorithm
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)    /// - `|x| ≤ 5`: Taylor power series (NIST DLMF 9.2.2)
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)    /// - `x > 5`: Olver asymptotic expansion (NIST DLMF 9.7.9–9.7.10)
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)    /// - `x < −5`: Oscillatory asymptotic (NIST DLMF 9.7.9, 9.7.11)
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)    pub fn airy_bi(x: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)        if x.abs() <= 5.0 {
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)            let (f, fp, g, gp) = taylor(x);
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)            (SQRT3 * (AI0 * f + C2 * g), SQRT3 * (AI0 * fp + C2 * gp))
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)        } else if x > 5.0 {
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)            // ζ = (2/3)x^{3/2}; Bi ~ e^{+ζ}/(√π x^{1/4})·Σ u_s/ζ^s  (no alternating sign)
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)            let zeta = 2.0 / 3.0 * x.powf(1.5);
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)            let x14 = x.powf(0.25);
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)            let ep = zeta.exp();
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)            let (_, _, un, vn) = asym_pos(zeta);
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)            (ep * un / (SQRTPI * x14), ep * x14 * vn / SQRTPI)
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)        } else {
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)            // θ = ζ + π/4; Bi(−z) = z^{−1/4}/√π·(cos θ·fe − sin θ·fo)
[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)            // Bi'(−z) = z^{1/4}/√π·(sin θ·ge + cos θ·go)
[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)            let t = -x;
[1428](https://docs.rs#1428)            let zeta = 2.0 / 3.0 * t.powf(1.5);
[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)            let t14 = t.powf(0.25);
[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)            let th = zeta + FRAC_PI_4;
[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)            let (s, c) = (th.sin(), th.cos());
