[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)            let (fe, fo, ge, go) = asym_neg(zeta);
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)            let bi = (c * fe - s * fo) / (SQRTPI * t14);
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)            let bip = t14 / SQRTPI * (s * ge + c * go);
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)            (bi, bip)
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)        }
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)    }
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)}
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)// ============================================================================
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)// ELLIPTIC FUNCTIONS
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)// ============================================================================
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)/// Elliptic integrals and functions
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)pub mod elliptic {
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)    /// Compute the complete elliptic integral of the first kind `K(m)`.
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)    ///
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)    /// # Algoritmo
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)    ///
[1451](https://docs.rs#1451)    /// ```text
[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)    /// K(m) = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - m \sin^2(t)}} dt
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)    /// ```
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)    /// Evaluated using the Arithmetic-Geometric Mean (AGM) method.
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)    ///
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)    /// # Precisión numérica
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)    ///
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)    /// AGM iterates until consecutive means converge within `1e-15` (up to 30 iterations).
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)    ///
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)    /// # Referencias
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)    ///
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §19.8.
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)    pub fn ellipk(m: f64) -> f64 {
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)        if !(0.0..1.0).contains(&m) {
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)            return f64::NAN;
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)        }
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)        if m == 0.0 {
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)            return std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
[1470](https://docs.rs#1470)        }
[1471](https://docs.rs#1471)
[1472](https://docs.rs#1472)        // Arithmetic-geometric mean method
[1473](https://docs.rs#1473)        let mut a = 1.0;
[1474](https://docs.rs#1474)        let mut b = (1.0 - m).sqrt();
[1475](https://docs.rs#1475)
[1476](https://docs.rs#1476)        for _ in 0..30 {
[1477](https://docs.rs#1477)            let a_new = (a + b) / 2.0;
[1478](https://docs.rs#1478)            let b_new = (a * b).sqrt();
[1479](https://docs.rs#1479)
[1480](https://docs.rs#1480)            if (a - b).abs() < 1e-15 {
[1481](https://docs.rs#1481)                break;
[1482](https://docs.rs#1482)            }
[1483](https://docs.rs#1483)
[1484](https://docs.rs#1484)            a = a_new;
[1485](https://docs.rs#1485)            b = b_new;
[1486](https://docs.rs#1486)        }
[1487](https://docs.rs#1487)
[1488](https://docs.rs#1488)        std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2 / a
[1489](https://docs.rs#1489)    }
[1490](https://docs.rs#1490)
[1491](https://docs.rs#1491)    /// Compute the complete elliptic integral of the second kind `E(m)`.
[1492](https://docs.rs#1492)    ///
[1493](https://docs.rs#1493)    /// # Algoritmo
[1494](https://docs.rs#1494)    ///
[1495](https://docs.rs#1495)    /// ```text
[1496](https://docs.rs#1496)    /// E(m) = \int_0^{\pi/2} \sqrt{1 - m \sin^2(t)} dt
[1497](https://docs.rs#1497)    /// ```
[1498](https://docs.rs#1498)    /// Evaluated using the Arithmetic-Geometric Mean (AGM) sequence combined with a summation property.
[1499](https://docs.rs#1499)    ///
[1500](https://docs.rs#1500)    /// # Precisión numérica
[1501](https://docs.rs#1501)    ///
[1502](https://docs.rs#1502)    /// AGM iterates until `c_n < 1e-15` (up to 30 iterations).
[1503](https://docs.rs#1503)    ///
[1504](https://docs.rs#1504)    /// # Referencias
[1505](https://docs.rs#1505)    ///
[1506](https://docs.rs#1506)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §19.8.
[1507](https://docs.rs#1507)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1508](https://docs.rs#1508)    pub fn ellipe(m: f64) -> f64 {
[1509](https://docs.rs#1509)        if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&m) {
[1510](https://docs.rs#1510)            return f64::NAN;
[1511](https://docs.rs#1511)        }
[1512](https://docs.rs#1512)        if m == 0.0 {
[1513](https://docs.rs#1513)            return std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
[1514](https://docs.rs#1514)        }
[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)        if m == 1.0 {
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)            return 1.0;
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)        }
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)        // AGM-based computation
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)        let mut a = 1.0;
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)        let mut b = (1.0 - m).sqrt();
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)        let mut _c = m.sqrt();
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)        let mut sum = 1.0 - m / 2.0;
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)        let mut pow2 = 1.0;
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)        for _ in 0..30 {
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)            let a_new = (a + b) / 2.0;
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)            let b_new = (a * b).sqrt();
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)            let c_new = (a - b) / 2.0;
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)            pow2 *= 2.0;
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)            sum -= pow2 * c_new * c_new;
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)            if c_new.abs() < 1e-15 {
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)                break;
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)            }
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)            a = a_new;
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)            b = b_new;
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)            _c = c_new;
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)        }
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)        sum * std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2 / a
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)    }
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)    /// Compute the incomplete elliptic integral of the first kind `F(\phi, m)`.
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)    ///
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)    /// # Algoritmo
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)    ///
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)    /// Expressed in terms of Carlson's symmetric form `R_F`.
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)    /// ```text
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)    /// F(\phi, m) = \sin(\phi) R_F(\cos^2\phi, 1 - m\sin^2\phi, 1)
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)    /// ```
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)    ///
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)    /// # Referencias
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)    ///
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)    /// - Carlson, B. C. (1995). Numerical computation of real or complex elliptic integrals.
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)    ///   *Numerical Algorithms*, 10(1), 13-26. DOI: [10.1007/BF02198293](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02198293)
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)    pub fn ellipf(phi: f64, m: f64) -> f64 {
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)        if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&m) {
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)            return f64::NAN;
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)        }
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)        // Carlson's RF
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)        let sin_phi = phi.sin();
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)        let cos_phi = phi.cos();
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)        let x = cos_phi * cos_phi;
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)        let y = 1.0 - m * sin_phi * sin_phi;
[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)        sin_phi * carlson_rf(x, y, 1.0)
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)    }
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)    /// Compute the incomplete elliptic integral of the second kind `E(\phi, m)`.
[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)    ///
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)    /// # Algoritmo
[1577](https://docs.rs#1577)    ///
[1578](https://docs.rs#1578)    /// Expressed in terms of Carlson's symmetric forms `R_F` and `R_D`.
[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)    /// ```text
[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)    /// E(\phi, m) = \sin(\phi) R_F(...) - \frac{m}{3} \sin^3(\phi) R_D(...)
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)    /// ```
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)    ///
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)    /// # Referencias
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)    ///
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)    /// - Carlson, B. C. (1995). Numerical computation of real or complex elliptic integrals.
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)    ///   *Numerical Algorithms*, 10(1), 13-26. DOI: [10.1007/BF02198293](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02198293)
[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)    pub fn ellipeinc(phi: f64, m: f64) -> f64 {
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)        if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&m) {
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)            return f64::NAN;
[1590](https://docs.rs#1590)        }
[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)
[1592](https://docs.rs#1592)        let sin_phi = phi.sin();
[1593](https://docs.rs#1593)        let cos_phi = phi.cos();
[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)
[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)        let x = cos_phi * cos_phi;
[1596](https://docs.rs#1596)        let y = 1.0 - m * sin_phi * sin_phi;
[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)        sin_phi * carlson_rf(x, y, 1.0) - (m / 3.0) * sin_phi.powi(3) * carlson_rd(x, y, 1.0)
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)    }
[1600](https://docs.rs#1600)
[1601](https://docs.rs#1601)    /// Compute Jacobi elliptic functions `(sn(u|m), cn(u|m), dn(u|m), am(u|m))`.
[1602](https://docs.rs#1602)    ///
[1603](https://docs.rs#1603)    /// REF: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §22.2 and §22.20
[1604](https://docs.rs#1604)    ///      https://dlmf.nist.gov/22
[1605](https://docs.rs#1605)    /// REF: Carlson, B. C. (1995) "Numerical computation of real or complex elliptic integrals"
[1606](https://docs.rs#1606)    ///      DOI: 10.1007/BF02198293
[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)    ///      Peer-reviewed: Numerical Algorithms, ISSN 1017-1398
[1608](https://docs.rs#1608)    ///      Validado contra: casos m=0, m=1 e identidades sn^2+cn^2=1, dn^2+m sn^2=1.
[1609](https://docs.rs#1609)    pub fn ellipj(u: f64, m: f64) -> (f64, f64, f64, f64) {
[1610](https://docs.rs#1610)        if !u.is_finite() || !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&m) {
[1611](https://docs.rs#1611)            return (f64::NAN, f64::NAN, f64::NAN, f64::NAN);
[1612](https://docs.rs#1612)        }
[1613](https://docs.rs#1613)        if m == 0.0 {
[1614](https://docs.rs#1614)            return (u.sin(), u.cos(), 1.0, u);
[1615](https://docs.rs#1615)        }
[1616](https://docs.rs#1616)        if m == 1.0 {
[1617](https://docs.rs#1617)            let sn = u.tanh();
[1618](https://docs.rs#1618)            let cn = 1.0 / u.cosh();
[1619](https://docs.rs#1619)            return (sn, cn, cn, sn.asin());
[1620](https://docs.rs#1620)        }
[1621](https://docs.rs#1621)
[1622](https://docs.rs#1622)        let k = ellipk(m);
[1623](https://docs.rs#1623)        let period = 4.0 * k;
[1624](https://docs.rs#1624)        let mut reduced = u.rem_euclid(period);
[1625](https://docs.rs#1625)        let (sign_sn, sign_cn) = if reduced <= k {
[1626](https://docs.rs#1626)            (1.0, 1.0)
[1627](https://docs.rs#1627)        } else if reduced <= 2.0 * k {
[1628](https://docs.rs#1628)            reduced = 2.0 * k - reduced;
[1629](https://docs.rs#1629)            (1.0, -1.0)
[1630](https://docs.rs#1630)        } else if reduced <= 3.0 * k {
[1631](https://docs.rs#1631)            reduced -= 2.0 * k;
[1632](https://docs.rs#1632)            (-1.0, -1.0)
[1633](https://docs.rs#1633)        } else {
[1634](https://docs.rs#1634)            reduced = 4.0 * k - reduced;
[1635](https://docs.rs#1635)            (-1.0, 1.0)
[1636](https://docs.rs#1636)        };
[1637](https://docs.rs#1637)
[1638](https://docs.rs#1638)        let amplitude = invert_ellipf_quadrant(reduced, m);
[1639](https://docs.rs#1639)        let sin_amp = amplitude.sin();
[1640](https://docs.rs#1640)        let cos_amp = amplitude.cos();
[1641](https://docs.rs#1641)        let sn = sign_sn * sin_amp;
[1642](https://docs.rs#1642)        let cn = sign_cn * cos_amp;
[1643](https://docs.rs#1643)        let dn = (1.0 - m * sin_amp * sin_amp).sqrt();
[1644](https://docs.rs#1644)        (sn, cn, dn, sn.asin())
[1645](https://docs.rs#1645)    }
[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)    fn invert_ellipf_quadrant(target: f64, m: f64) -> f64 {
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)        if target == 0.0 {
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)            return 0.0;
[1650](https://docs.rs#1650)        }
[1651](https://docs.rs#1651)        let mut lo = 0.0;
[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)        let mut hi = std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)        for _ in 0..80 {
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)            let mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi);
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)            if ellipf(mid, m) < target {
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)                lo = mid;
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)            } else {
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)                hi = mid;
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)            }
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)        }
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)        0.5 * (lo + hi)
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)    }
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)    /// Evaluate Carlson's symmetric elliptic integral `R_F(x, y, z)`.
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)    ///
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)    /// # Algoritmo
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)    ///
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)    /// Uses duplication theorem iterates.
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)    ///
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)    /// # Precisión numérica
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)    ///
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)    /// The maximum of 30 iterations is executed until convergence tolerance `< 1e-10` is hit.
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)    ///
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)    /// # Referencias
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)    ///
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)    /// - Carlson, B. C. (1995). Numerical computation of real or complex elliptic integrals.
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)    ///   *Numerical Algorithms*, 10(1), 13-26. DOI: [10.1007/BF02198293](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02198293)
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)    fn carlson_rf(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> f64 {
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)        let mut xn = x;
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)        let mut yn = y;
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)        let mut zn = z;
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)        for _ in 0..30 {
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)            let lambda = (xn * yn).sqrt() + (yn * zn).sqrt() + (zn * xn).sqrt();
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)            xn = (xn + lambda) / 4.0;
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)            yn = (yn + lambda) / 4.0;
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)            zn = (zn + lambda) / 4.0;
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)            let avg = (xn + yn + zn) / 3.0;
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)            let dx = 1.0 - xn / avg;
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)            let dy = 1.0 - yn / avg;
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)            let dz = 1.0 - zn / avg;
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)            if dx.abs().max(dy.abs()).max(dz.abs()) < 1e-10 {
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)                let e2 = dx * dy + dy * dz + dz * dx;
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)                let e3 = dx * dy * dz;
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)                return (1.0 - e2 / 10.0 + e3 / 14.0 + e2 * e2 / 24.0 - 3.0 * e2 * e3 / 44.0)
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)                    / avg.sqrt();
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)            }
[1700](https://docs.rs#1700)        }
[1701](https://docs.rs#1701)
[1702](https://docs.rs#1702)        1.0 / ((xn + yn + zn) / 3.0).sqrt()
[1703](https://docs.rs#1703)    }
[1704](https://docs.rs#1704)
[1705](https://docs.rs#1705)    /// Evaluate Carlson's symmetric elliptic integral `R_D(x, y, z)`.
[1706](https://docs.rs#1706)    ///
[1707](https://docs.rs#1707)    /// # Algoritmo
[1708](https://docs.rs#1708)    ///
[1709](https://docs.rs#1709)    /// Evaluated using duplication theorem iterations.
[1710](https://docs.rs#1710)    ///
[1711](https://docs.rs#1711)    /// # Precisión numérica
[1712](https://docs.rs#1712)    ///
[1713](https://docs.rs#1713)    /// Reaches a stable state defined by `tolerance < 1e-10`.
[1714](https://docs.rs#1714)    ///
[1715](https://docs.rs#1715)    /// # Referencias
[1716](https://docs.rs#1716)    ///
[1717](https://docs.rs#1717)    /// - Carlson, B. C. (1995). Numerical computation of real or complex elliptic integrals.
[1718](https://docs.rs#1718)    ///   *Numerical Algorithms*, 10(1), 13-26. DOI: [10.1007/BF02198293](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02198293)
[1719](https://docs.rs#1719)    fn carlson_rd(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> f64 {
[1720](https://docs.rs#1720)        let mut xn = x;
[1721](https://docs.rs#1721)        let mut yn = y;
[1722](https://docs.rs#1722)        let mut zn = z;
[1723](https://docs.rs#1723)        let mut sum = 0.0;
[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)        let mut pow4 = 1.0;
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)        for _ in 0..30 {
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)            let lambda = (xn * yn).sqrt() + (yn * zn).sqrt() + (zn * xn).sqrt();
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)            sum += pow4 / (zn.sqrt() * (zn + lambda));
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)            pow4 /= 4.0;
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)            xn = (xn + lambda) / 4.0;
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)            yn = (yn + lambda) / 4.0;
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)            zn = (zn + lambda) / 4.0;
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)            let avg = (xn + yn + 3.0 * zn) / 5.0;
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)            let dx = 1.0 - xn / avg;
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)            let dy = 1.0 - yn / avg;
[1737](https://docs.rs#1737)            let dz = 1.0 - zn / avg;
[1738](https://docs.rs#1738)
[1739](https://docs.rs#1739)            if dx.abs().max(dy.abs()).max(dz.abs()) < 1e-10 {
[1740](https://docs.rs#1740)                let e2 = dx * dy + dy * dz + dz * dx;
[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)                let e3 = dx * dy * dz;
[1742](https://docs.rs#1742)                let e4 = dx * dx * (dy * dy + dz * dz);
[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)                let e5 = dx * dx * dy * dz;
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)                return 3.0 * sum
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)                    + pow4
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)                        * avg.powf(-1.5)
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748)                        * (1.0 - 3.0 * e2 / 14.0 + e3 / 6.0 + 9.0 * e2 * e2 / 88.0
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)                            - 3.0 * e4 / 22.0
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)                            - 9.0 * e2 * e3 / 52.0
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)                            + 3.0 * e5 / 26.0);
[1752](https://docs.rs#1752)            }
[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)        }
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)        3.0 * sum
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)    }
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)}
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)// ============================================================================
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)// ORTHOGONAL POLYNOMIALS
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)// ============================================================================
[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)
[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)/// Orthogonal polynomials (Legendre, Hermite, Laguerre, Chebyshev)
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)pub mod orthopoly {
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)    /// Compute the Legendre polynomial `P_n(x)`.
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)    ///
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)    /// # Algoritmo
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)    ///
[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)    /// Evaluated using Bonnet's recursion formula:
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)    /// ```text
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)    /// (n+1) P_{n+1}(x) = (2n+1) x P_n(x) - n P_{n-1}(x)
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)    /// ```
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)    ///
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)    /// # Referencias
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)    ///
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §18.9.
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)    pub fn legendre_p(n: usize, x: f64) -> f64 {
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)        if n == 0 {
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)            return 1.0;
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)        }
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)        if n == 1 {
[1784](https://docs.rs#1784)            return x;
[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)        }
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)        // Recurrence: (n+1)*P_{n+1} = (2n+1)*x*P_n - n*P_{n-1}
[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)        let mut p_prev = 1.0;
[1789](https://docs.rs#1789)        let mut p_curr = x;
[1790](https://docs.rs#1790)
[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)        for k in 1..n {
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)            let p_next = ((2 * k + 1) as f64 * x * p_curr - k as f64 * p_prev) / (k + 1) as f64;
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)            p_prev = p_curr;
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)            p_curr = p_next;
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)        }
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)        p_curr
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)    }
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)    /// Compute the associated Legendre polynomial `P_n^m(x)`.
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)    ///
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)    /// # Algoritmo
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)    ///
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)    /// Generates values using recursive relations across degrees `n` starting from `P_m^m(x)`.
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)    ///
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)    /// # Referencias
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)    ///
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §14.7.
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)    pub fn legendre_p_assoc(n: usize, m: usize, x: f64) -> f64 {
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)        if m > n {
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)            return 0.0;
[1813](https://docs.rs#1813)        }
[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)
[1815](https://docs.rs#1815)        // P_m^m(x) = (-1)^m * (2m-1)!! * (1-x^2)^(m/2)
[1816](https://docs.rs#1816)        let pmm = if m == 0 {
[1817](https://docs.rs#1817)            1.0
[1818](https://docs.rs#1818)        } else {
[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)            let sign = if m.is_multiple_of(2) { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)            let factor = (1..=m).map(|i| (2 * i - 1) as f64).product::<f64>();
[1821](https://docs.rs#1821)            sign * factor * (1.0 - x * x).powf(m as f64 / 2.0)
[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)        };
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)        if n == m {
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)            return pmm;
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)        }
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)        // P_{m+1}^m = x * (2m+1) * P_m^m
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)        let pmm1 = x * (2 * m + 1) as f64 * pmm;
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)        if n == m + 1 {
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)            return pmm1;
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)        }
[1833](https://docs.rs#1833)
[1834](https://docs.rs#1834)        // Recurrence
[1835](https://docs.rs#1835)        let mut p_prev = pmm;
[1836](https://docs.rs#1836)        let mut p_curr = pmm1;
[1837](https://docs.rs#1837)
[1838](https://docs.rs#1838)        for l in (m + 2)..=n {
[1839](https://docs.rs#1839)            let p_next = (((2 * l - 1) as f64 * x * p_curr) - ((l + m - 1) as f64 * p_prev))
[1840](https://docs.rs#1840)                / (l - m) as f64;
[1841](https://docs.rs#1841)            p_prev = p_curr;
[1842](https://docs.rs#1842)            p_curr = p_next;
[1843](https://docs.rs#1843)        }
[1844](https://docs.rs#1844)
[1845](https://docs.rs#1845)        p_curr
[1846](https://docs.rs#1846)    }
[1847](https://docs.rs#1847)
[1848](https://docs.rs#1848)    /// Real spherical harmonic `Y_l^m(θ, φ)` (orthonormal convention), built on
[1849](https://docs.rs#1849)    /// the associated Legendre function. `θ` is colatitude, `φ` azimuth.
[1850](https://docs.rs#1850)    ///
[1851](https://docs.rs#1851)    /// Standard real basis:
[1852](https://docs.rs#1852)    /// - `m = 0`:  `K_l^0 · P_l^0(cos θ)`
[1853](https://docs.rs#1853)    /// - `m > 0`:  `√2 · K_l^m · P_l^m(cos θ) · cos(m φ)`
[1854](https://docs.rs#1854)    /// - `m < 0`:  `√2 · K_l^{|m|} · P_l^{|m|}(cos θ) · sin(|m| φ)`
[1855](https://docs.rs#1855)    ///
[1856](https://docs.rs#1856)    /// with `K_l^m = √[ (2l+1)/(4π) · (l−m)!/(l+m)! ]`. The Condon–Shortley phase
[1857](https://docs.rs#1857)    /// carried by [`legendre_p_assoc`] is removed, so `Y_1^{+1} ∝ +sin θ cos φ`
[1858](https://docs.rs#1858)    /// (the real `p_x` orbital).
[1859](https://docs.rs#1859)    ///
[1860](https://docs.rs#1860)    /// # Referencias
[1861](https://docs.rs#1861)    ///
[1862](https://docs.rs#1862)    /// - NIST DLMF §14.30 (spherical harmonics).
[1863](https://docs.rs#1863)    pub fn sph_harm_real(l: usize, m: i32, theta: f64, phi: f64) -> f64 {
[1864](https://docs.rs#1864)        let am = m.unsigned_abs() as usize;
[1865](https://docs.rs#1865)        if am > l {
[1866](https://docs.rs#1866)            return 0.0;
[1867](https://docs.rs#1867)        }
[1868](https://docs.rs#1868)        // (l−am)! / (l+am)! = 1 / ∏_{k=l−am+1}^{l+am} k.
[1869](https://docs.rs#1869)        let mut ratio = 1.0;
[1870](https://docs.rs#1870)        for k in (l - am + 1)..=(l + am) {
[1871](https://docs.rs#1871)            ratio /= k as f64;
[1872](https://docs.rs#1872)        }
[1873](https://docs.rs#1873)        let k_norm = ((2 * l + 1) as f64 / (4.0 * std::f64::consts::PI) * ratio).sqrt();
[1874](https://docs.rs#1874)        // Remove the Condon–Shortley phase that legendre_p_assoc carries.
[1875](https://docs.rs#1875)        let cs = if am.is_multiple_of(2) { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
[1876](https://docs.rs#1876)        let plm = cs * legendre_p_assoc(l, am, theta.cos());
[1877](https://docs.rs#1877)        if m > 0 {
[1878](https://docs.rs#1878)            std::f64::consts::SQRT_2 * k_norm * plm * ((am as f64) * phi).cos()
[1879](https://docs.rs#1879)        } else if m < 0 {
[1880](https://docs.rs#1880)            std::f64::consts::SQRT_2 * k_norm * plm * ((am as f64) * phi).sin()
[1881](https://docs.rs#1881)        } else {
[1882](https://docs.rs#1882)            k_norm * plm
[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)        }
[1884](https://docs.rs#1884)    }
[1885](https://docs.rs#1885)
[1886](https://docs.rs#1886)    /// Compute the physicist's Hermite polynomial `H_n(x)`.
[1887](https://docs.rs#1887)    ///
[1888](https://docs.rs#1888)    /// # Algoritmo
[1889](https://docs.rs#1889)    ///
[1890](https://docs.rs#1890)    /// Generated using the specific three-term recurrence relation:
[1891](https://docs.rs#1891)    /// ```text
[1892](https://docs.rs#1892)    /// H_{n+1}(x) = 2x H_n(x) - 2n H_{n-1}(x)
[1893](https://docs.rs#1893)    /// ```
[1894](https://docs.rs#1894)    ///
[1895](https://docs.rs#1895)    /// # Referencias
[1896](https://docs.rs#1896)    ///
[1897](https://docs.rs#1897)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §18.9.
[1898](https://docs.rs#1898)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1899](https://docs.rs#1899)    pub fn hermite_h(n: usize, x: f64) -> f64 {
[1900](https://docs.rs#1900)        if n == 0 {
[1901](https://docs.rs#1901)            return 1.0;
[1902](https://docs.rs#1902)        }
[1903](https://docs.rs#1903)        if n == 1 {
[1904](https://docs.rs#1904)            return 2.0 * x;
[1905](https://docs.rs#1905)        }
[1906](https://docs.rs#1906)
[1907](https://docs.rs#1907)        // Recurrence: H_{n+1} = 2x*H_n - 2n*H_{n-1}
[1908](https://docs.rs#1908)        let mut h_prev = 1.0;
[1909](https://docs.rs#1909)        let mut h_curr = 2.0 * x;
[1910](https://docs.rs#1910)
[1911](https://docs.rs#1911)        for k in 1..n {
[1912](https://docs.rs#1912)            let h_next = 2.0 * x * h_curr - 2.0 * k as f64 * h_prev;
[1913](https://docs.rs#1913)            h_prev = h_curr;
[1914](https://docs.rs#1914)            h_curr = h_next;
[1915](https://docs.rs#1915)        }
[1916](https://docs.rs#1916)
[1917](https://docs.rs#1917)        h_curr
[1918](https://docs.rs#1918)    }
[1919](https://docs.rs#1919)
[1920](https://docs.rs#1920)    /// Compute the probabilist's Hermite polynomial `He_n(x)`.
[1921](https://docs.rs#1921)    ///
[1922](https://docs.rs#1922)    /// # Algoritmo
[1923](https://docs.rs#1923)    ///
[1924](https://docs.rs#1924)    /// Generated using the explicit recurrence:
[1925](https://docs.rs#1925)    /// ```text
[1926](https://docs.rs#1926)    /// He_{n+1}(x) = x He_n(x) - n He_{n-1}(x)
[1927](https://docs.rs#1927)    /// ```
[1928](https://docs.rs#1928)    ///
[1929](https://docs.rs#1929)    /// # Referencias
[1930](https://docs.rs#1930)    ///
[1931](https://docs.rs#1931)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §18.9.
[1932](https://docs.rs#1932)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1933](https://docs.rs#1933)    pub fn hermite_he(n: usize, x: f64) -> f64 {
[1934](https://docs.rs#1934)        if n == 0 {
[1935](https://docs.rs#1935)            return 1.0;
[1936](https://docs.rs#1936)        }
[1937](https://docs.rs#1937)        if n == 1 {
[1938](https://docs.rs#1938)            return x;
[1939](https://docs.rs#1939)        }
[1940](https://docs.rs#1940)
[1941](https://docs.rs#1941)        // Recurrence: He_{n+1} = x*He_n - n*He_{n-1}
[1942](https://docs.rs#1942)        let mut h_prev = 1.0;
[1943](https://docs.rs#1943)        let mut h_curr = x;
[1944](https://docs.rs#1944)
[1945](https://docs.rs#1945)        for k in 1..n {
[1946](https://docs.rs#1946)            let h_next = x * h_curr - k as f64 * h_prev;
[1947](https://docs.rs#1947)            h_prev = h_curr;
[1948](https://docs.rs#1948)            h_curr = h_next;
[1949](https://docs.rs#1949)        }
[1950](https://docs.rs#1950)
[1951](https://docs.rs#1951)        h_curr
[1952](https://docs.rs#1952)    }
[1953](https://docs.rs#1953)
[1954](https://docs.rs#1954)    /// Compute the Laguerre polynomial `L_n(x)`.
[1955](https://docs.rs#1955)    ///
[1956](https://docs.rs#1956)    /// # Algoritmo
[1957](https://docs.rs#1957)    ///
[1958](https://docs.rs#1958)    /// Evaluated using the fundamental recurrence relation:
[1959](https://docs.rs#1959)    /// ```text
[1960](https://docs.rs#1960)    /// (n+1) L_{n+1}(x) = (2n+1-x) L_n(x) - n L_{n-1}(x)
[1961](https://docs.rs#1961)    /// ```
[1962](https://docs.rs#1962)    ///
[1963](https://docs.rs#1963)    /// # Referencias
[1964](https://docs.rs#1964)    ///
[1965](https://docs.rs#1965)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §18.9.
[1966](https://docs.rs#1966)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1967](https://docs.rs#1967)    pub fn laguerre_l(n: usize, x: f64) -> f64 {
[1968](https://docs.rs#1968)        if n == 0 {
[1969](https://docs.rs#1969)            return 1.0;
[1970](https://docs.rs#1970)        }
[1971](https://docs.rs#1971)        if n == 1 {
[1972](https://docs.rs#1972)            return 1.0 - x;
[1973](https://docs.rs#1973)        }
[1974](https://docs.rs#1974)
[1975](https://docs.rs#1975)        // Recurrence: (n+1)*L_{n+1} = (2n+1-x)*L_n - n*L_{n-1}
[1976](https://docs.rs#1976)        let mut l_prev = 1.0;
[1977](https://docs.rs#1977)        let mut l_curr = 1.0 - x;
[1978](https://docs.rs#1978)
[1979](https://docs.rs#1979)        for k in 1..n {
[1980](https://docs.rs#1980)            let l_next = ((2 * k + 1) as f64 - x) * l_curr / (k + 1) as f64
[1981](https://docs.rs#1981)                - k as f64 * l_prev / (k + 1) as f64;
[1982](https://docs.rs#1982)            l_prev = l_curr;
[1983](https://docs.rs#1983)            l_curr = l_next;
[1984](https://docs.rs#1984)        }
[1985](https://docs.rs#1985)
[1986](https://docs.rs#1986)        l_curr
[1987](https://docs.rs#1987)    }
[1988](https://docs.rs#1988)
[1989](https://docs.rs#1989)    /// Compute the associated Laguerre polynomial `L_n^{(\alpha)}(x)`.
[1990](https://docs.rs#1990)    ///
[1991](https://docs.rs#1991)    /// # Algoritmo
[1992](https://docs.rs#1992)    ///
[1993](https://docs.rs#1993)    /// Evaluated recursively based on parameter `\alpha`.
[1994](https://docs.rs#1994)    ///
[1995](https://docs.rs#1995)    /// # Referencias
[1996](https://docs.rs#1996)    ///
[1997](https://docs.rs#1997)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §18.9.
[1998](https://docs.rs#1998)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[1999](https://docs.rs#1999)    pub fn laguerre_l_assoc(n: usize, alpha: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[2000](https://docs.rs#2000)        if n == 0 {
[2001](https://docs.rs#2001)            return 1.0;
[2002](https://docs.rs#2002)        }
[2003](https://docs.rs#2003)        if n == 1 {
[2004](https://docs.rs#2004)            return 1.0 + alpha - x;
[2005](https://docs.rs#2005)        }
[2006](https://docs.rs#2006)
[2007](https://docs.rs#2007)        let mut l_prev = 1.0;
[2008](https://docs.rs#2008)        let mut l_curr = 1.0 + alpha - x;
[2009](https://docs.rs#2009)
[2010](https://docs.rs#2010)        for k in 1..n {
[2011](https://docs.rs#2011)            let l_next = ((2 * k + 1) as f64 + alpha - x) * l_curr / (k + 1) as f64
[2012](https://docs.rs#2012)                - (k as f64 + alpha) * l_prev / (k + 1) as f64;
[2013](https://docs.rs#2013)            l_prev = l_curr;
[2014](https://docs.rs#2014)            l_curr = l_next;
[2015](https://docs.rs#2015)        }
[2016](https://docs.rs#2016)
[2017](https://docs.rs#2017)        l_curr
[2018](https://docs.rs#2018)    }
[2019](https://docs.rs#2019)
[2020](https://docs.rs#2020)    /// Compute the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind `T_n(x)`.
[2021](https://docs.rs#2021)    ///
[2022](https://docs.rs#2022)    /// # Algoritmo
[2023](https://docs.rs#2023)    ///
[2024](https://docs.rs#2024)    /// Evaluated via recurrence relation:
[2025](https://docs.rs#2025)    /// ```text
[2026](https://docs.rs#2026)    /// T_{n+1}(x) = 2x T_n(x) - T_{n-1}(x)
[2027](https://docs.rs#2027)    /// ```
[2028](https://docs.rs#2028)    ///
[2029](https://docs.rs#2029)    /// # Referencias
[2030](https://docs.rs#2030)    ///
[2031](https://docs.rs#2031)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §18.9.
[2032](https://docs.rs#2032)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[2033](https://docs.rs#2033)    pub fn chebyshev_t(n: usize, x: f64) -> f64 {
[2034](https://docs.rs#2034)        if n == 0 {
[2035](https://docs.rs#2035)            return 1.0;
[2036](https://docs.rs#2036)        }
[2037](https://docs.rs#2037)        if n == 1 {
[2038](https://docs.rs#2038)            return x;
[2039](https://docs.rs#2039)        }
[2040](https://docs.rs#2040)
[2041](https://docs.rs#2041)        // Recurrence: T_{n+1} = 2x*T_n - T_{n-1}
[2042](https://docs.rs#2042)        let mut t_prev = 1.0;
[2043](https://docs.rs#2043)        let mut t_curr = x;
[2044](https://docs.rs#2044)
[2045](https://docs.rs#2045)        for _ in 1..n {
[2046](https://docs.rs#2046)            let t_next = 2.0 * x * t_curr - t_prev;
[2047](https://docs.rs#2047)            t_prev = t_curr;
[2048](https://docs.rs#2048)            t_curr = t_next;
[2049](https://docs.rs#2049)        }
[2050](https://docs.rs#2050)
[2051](https://docs.rs#2051)        t_curr
[2052](https://docs.rs#2052)    }
[2053](https://docs.rs#2053)
[2054](https://docs.rs#2054)    /// Compute the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind `U_n(x)`.
[2055](https://docs.rs#2055)    ///
[2056](https://docs.rs#2056)    /// # Algoritmo
[2057](https://docs.rs#2057)    ///
[2058](https://docs.rs#2058)    /// Evaluated via recurrence relation:
[2059](https://docs.rs#2059)    /// ```text
[2060](https://docs.rs#2060)    /// U_{n+1}(x) = 2x U_n(x) - U_{n-1}(x)
[2061](https://docs.rs#2061)    /// ```
[2062](https://docs.rs#2062)    ///
[2063](https://docs.rs#2063)    /// # Referencias
[2064](https://docs.rs#2064)    ///
[2065](https://docs.rs#2065)    /// - NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. §18.9.
[2066](https://docs.rs#2066)    ///   DOI: [10.6028/jres.069b.001](https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.069b.001)
[2067](https://docs.rs#2067)    pub fn chebyshev_u(n: usize, x: f64) -> f64 {
[2068](https://docs.rs#2068)        if n == 0 {
[2069](https://docs.rs#2069)            return 1.0;
[2070](https://docs.rs#2070)        }
[2071](https://docs.rs#2071)        if n == 1 {
[2072](https://docs.rs#2072)            return 2.0 * x;
[2073](https://docs.rs#2073)        }
[2074](https://docs.rs#2074)
[2075](https://docs.rs#2075)        // Recurrence: U_{n+1} = 2x*U_n - U_{n-1}
[2076](https://docs.rs#2076)        let mut u_prev = 1.0;
[2077](https://docs.rs#2077)        let mut u_curr = 2.0 * x;
[2078](https://docs.rs#2078)
[2079](https://docs.rs#2079)        for _ in 1..n {
[2080](https://docs.rs#2080)            let u_next = 2.0 * x * u_curr - u_prev;
[2081](https://docs.rs#2081)            u_prev = u_curr;
[2082](https://docs.rs#2082)            u_curr = u_next;
[2083](https://docs.rs#2083)        }
[2084](https://docs.rs#2084)
[2085](https://docs.rs#2085)        u_curr
[2086](https://docs.rs#2086)    }
[2087](https://docs.rs#2087)}
[2088](https://docs.rs#2088)
[2089](https://docs.rs#2089)// ============================================================================
[2090](https://docs.rs#2090)// LAMBERT W FUNCTION
[2091](https://docs.rs#2091)// ============================================================================
[2092](https://docs.rs#2092)
[2093](https://docs.rs#2093)/// Lambert W function (principal branch W₀).
[2094](https://docs.rs#2094)pub mod lambertw_funcs {
[2095](https://docs.rs#2095)    use super::{SpecialError, SpecialResult};
[2096](https://docs.rs#2096)
[2097](https://docs.rs#2097)    /// Principal branch of the Lambert W function, W₀(z).
[2098](https://docs.rs#2098)    ///
[2099](https://docs.rs#2099)    /// Solves W·eᵂ = z for real z ≥ -1/e (where W ≥ -1).
[2100](https://docs.rs#2100)    /// Invariant: `W(z)·exp(W(z)) ≈ z` to machine precision.
[2101](https://docs.rs#2101)    ///
[2102](https://docs.rs#2102)    /// # References
[2103](https://docs.rs#2103)    /// - Corless, R. M., et al. (1996). On the Lambert W function.
[2104](https://docs.rs#2104)    ///   *Adv. Comput. Math.* 5, 329–359. DOI: 10.1007/BF02124750
[2105](https://docs.rs#2105)    pub fn lambertw(z: f64) -> SpecialResult<f64> {
[2106](https://docs.rs#2106)        const BRANCH_POINT: f64 = -std::f64::consts::E;
[2107](https://docs.rs#2107)        // -1/e ≈ -0.36787944...
[2108](https://docs.rs#2108)        let limit = 1.0 / BRANCH_POINT.abs(); // = 1/e
[2109](https://docs.rs#2109)        if z < -limit {
[2110](https://docs.rs#2110)            return Err(SpecialError::DomainError(format!(
[2111](https://docs.rs#2111)                "lambertw: z={z} < -1/e; principal branch undefined"
[2112](https://docs.rs#2112)            )));
[2113](https://docs.rs#2113)        }
[2114](https://docs.rs#2114)        if z == 0.0 {
[2115](https://docs.rs#2115)            return Ok(0.0);
[2116](https://docs.rs#2116)        }
[2117](https://docs.rs#2117)
[2118](https://docs.rs#2118)        // Initial guess (log-based for large z, series near branch point, linear near 0)
[2119](https://docs.rs#2119)        // Note: must be z > 1 (strict) — at z=1, lz=0 → lz.ln()=-∞ → diverges.
[2120](https://docs.rs#2120)        let mut w: f64 = if z > 1.0 {
[2121](https://docs.rs#2121)            let lz = z.ln();
[2122](https://docs.rs#2122)            lz - lz.ln()
[2123](https://docs.rs#2123)        } else if z > -limit * 0.99 && z < 0.0 {
[2124](https://docs.rs#2124)            // Near branch point: W ≈ -1 + t where t = sqrt(2(ez+1))
[2125](https://docs.rs#2125)            let t = (2.0 * (1.0 + std::f64::consts::E * z)).max(0.0).sqrt();
[2126](https://docs.rs#2126)            -1.0 + t
[2127](https://docs.rs#2127)        } else {
[2128](https://docs.rs#2128)            z
[2129](https://docs.rs#2129)        };
[2130](https://docs.rs#2130)
[2131](https://docs.rs#2131)        // Halley iteration (cubic convergence)
[2132](https://docs.rs#2132)        // f(w) = w·eʷ - z = 0,  f' = eʷ(w+1),  f''/2f' = (w+2)/(2(w+1))
[2133](https://docs.rs#2133)        for _ in 0..60 {
[2134](https://docs.rs#2134)            let ew = w.exp();
[2135](https://docs.rs#2135)            let f = w * ew - z;
[2136](https://docs.rs#2136)            if f.abs() < 1e-15 * (z.abs() + 1e-300) {
[2137](https://docs.rs#2137)                break;
[2138](https://docs.rs#2138)            }
[2139](https://docs.rs#2139)            let wp1 = w + 1.0;
[2140](https://docs.rs#2140)            // Guard: Halley denominator degenerates at w = -1
[2141](https://docs.rs#2141)            let halley_den = wp1 - (w + 2.0) * f / (2.0 * wp1);
[2142](https://docs.rs#2142)            if halley_den.abs() < 1e-15 {
[2143](https://docs.rs#2143)                break;
[2144](https://docs.rs#2144)            }
[2145](https://docs.rs#2145)            w -= f / (ew * halley_den);
[2146](https://docs.rs#2146)        }
[2147](https://docs.rs#2147)
[2148](https://docs.rs#2148)        Ok(w)
[2149](https://docs.rs#2149)    }
[2150](https://docs.rs#2150)}
[2151](https://docs.rs#2151)
[2152](https://docs.rs#2152)// ============================================================================
[2153](https://docs.rs#2153)// RIEMANN ZETA FUNCTION
[2154](https://docs.rs#2154)// ============================================================================
[2155](https://docs.rs#2155)
[2156](https://docs.rs#2156)/// Riemann zeta and Hurwitz zeta functions.
[2157](https://docs.rs#2157)pub mod zeta_funcs {
[2158](https://docs.rs#2158)    use super::gamma_funcs;
[2159](https://docs.rs#2159)
[2160](https://docs.rs#2160)    // Bernoulli numbers B_{2k} for k=1..8 (A&S Table 23.2)
[2161](https://docs.rs#2161)    const BERNOULLI_2K: [f64; 8] = [
[2162](https://docs.rs#2162)        1.0 / 6.0,
[2163](https://docs.rs#2163)        -1.0 / 30.0,
[2164](https://docs.rs#2164)        1.0 / 42.0,
[2165](https://docs.rs#2165)        -1.0 / 30.0,
[2166](https://docs.rs#2166)        5.0 / 66.0,
[2167](https://docs.rs#2167)        -691.0 / 2730.0,
[2168](https://docs.rs#2168)        7.0 / 6.0,
[2169](https://docs.rs#2169)        -3617.0 / 510.0,
[2170](https://docs.rs#2170)    ];
[2171](https://docs.rs#2171)    // Factorial (2k)! for k=1..8
[2172](https://docs.rs#2172)    const FACT_2K: [f64; 8] = [2.0, 24.0, 720.0, 40320.0, 3628800.0, 479001600.0, 87178291200.0, 20922789888000.0];
[2173](https://docs.rs#2173)
[2174](https://docs.rs#2174)    /// Riemann zeta function ζ(s) via Euler–Maclaurin (s > 1),
[2175](https://docs.rs#2175)    /// functional equation (s < 0), and eta transform (0 < s < 1).
[2176](https://docs.rs#2176)    ///
[2177](https://docs.rs#2177)    /// Returns `NaN` at the pole s = 1 and for `0 < s ≤ 1` in reduced precision
[2178](https://docs.rs#2178)    /// (use s > 1 for full machine precision).
[2179](https://docs.rs#2179)    ///
[2180](https://docs.rs#2180)    /// # References
[2181](https://docs.rs#2181)    /// - NIST DLMF §25.2. DOI: 10.6028/jres.069b.001
[2182](https://docs.rs#2182)    /// - Abramowitz & Stegun §23.2.
[2183](https://docs.rs#2183)    pub fn zeta(s: f64) -> f64 {
[2184](https://docs.rs#2184)        if s == 1.0 {
[2185](https://docs.rs#2185)            return f64::NAN; // pole
[2186](https://docs.rs#2186)        }
[2187](https://docs.rs#2187)        if s > 1.0 {
[2188](https://docs.rs#2188)            return euler_maclaurin(s);
[2189](https://docs.rs#2189)        }
[2190](https://docs.rs#2190)        if s == 0.0 {
[2191](https://docs.rs#2191)            return -0.5; // ζ(0) = -1/2 (analytic continuation)
[2192](https://docs.rs#2192)        }
[2193](https://docs.rs#2193)        if s < 0.0 {
[2194](https://docs.rs#2194)            // Functional equation: ζ(s) = 2^s π^{s-1} sin(πs/2) Γ(1-s) ζ(1-s)
[2195](https://docs.rs#2195)            let one_minus_s = 1.0 - s; // > 1
[2196](https://docs.rs#2196)            let sin_term = (s * std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2).sin();
[2197](https://docs.rs#2197)            if sin_term.abs() < 1e-300 {
[2198](https://docs.rs#2198)                // Trivial zero at negative even integers: ζ(-2k) = 0
[2199](https://docs.rs#2199)                return 0.0;
[2200](https://docs.rs#2200)            }
[2201](https://docs.rs#2201)            return 2.0_f64.powf(s)
[2202](https://docs.rs#2202)                * std::f64::consts::PI.powf(s - 1.0)
[2203](https://docs.rs#2203)                * sin_term
[2204](https://docs.rs#2204)                * gamma_funcs::gamma(one_minus_s)
[2205](https://docs.rs#2205)                * euler_maclaurin(one_minus_s);
[2206](https://docs.rs#2206)        }
[2207](https://docs.rs#2207)        // 0 < s < 1: use Dirichlet eta η(s) = ζ(s)·(1 - 2^{1-s})
[2208](https://docs.rs#2208)        let eta = euler_eta(s);
[2209](https://docs.rs#2209)        let factor = 1.0 - 2.0_f64.powf(1.0 - s);
[2210](https://docs.rs#2210)        if factor.abs() < 1e-15 {
[2211](https://docs.rs#2211)            return f64::NAN; // numeric degeneration near s=1 from the left
[2212](https://docs.rs#2212)        }
[2213](https://docs.rs#2213)        eta / factor
[2214](https://docs.rs#2214)    }
[2215](https://docs.rs#2215)
[2216](https://docs.rs#2216)    /// Hurwitz zeta function ζ(s, q) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ (n+q)^{-s}, valid for s > 1 and q > 0.
[2217](https://docs.rs#2217)    pub fn zeta_hurwitz(s: f64, q: f64) -> f64 {
[2218](https://docs.rs#2218)        if s <= 1.0 || q <= 0.0 {
[2219](https://docs.rs#2219)            return f64::NAN;
[2220](https://docs.rs#2220)        }
[2221](https://docs.rs#2221)        euler_maclaurin_hurwitz(s, q)
[2222](https://docs.rs#2222)    }
[2223](https://docs.rs#2223)
[2224](https://docs.rs#2224)    // Euler–Maclaurin for ζ(s, q) = Σ_{n=0}^{N-1}(n+q)^{-s} + tail via EM formula
[2225](https://docs.rs#2225)    fn euler_maclaurin_hurwitz(s: f64, q: f64) -> f64 {
[2226](https://docs.rs#2226)        const N: usize = 100;
[2227](https://docs.rs#2227)        let mut sum = 0.0_f64;
[2228](https://docs.rs#2228)        for n in 0..N {
[2229](https://docs.rs#2229)            sum += (n as f64 + q).powf(-s);
[2230](https://docs.rs#2230)        }
[2231](https://docs.rs#2231)        let nq = N as f64 + q;
[2232](https://docs.rs#2232)        sum += nq.powf(1.0 - s) / (s - 1.0); // integral tail
[2233](https://docs.rs#2233)        sum += 0.5 * nq.powf(-s); // half-term correction
[2234](https://docs.rs#2234)        let mut nq_pow = nq.powf(-(s + 1.0));
[2235](https://docs.rs#2235)        let mut spow = s;
[2236](https://docs.rs#2236)        for k in 0..8 {
[2237](https://docs.rs#2237)            let correction = BERNOULLI_2K[k] / FACT_2K[k] * spow * nq_pow;
[2238](https://docs.rs#2238)            if correction.abs() < 1e-17 * sum.abs() {
[2239](https://docs.rs#2239)                break;
[2240](https://docs.rs#2240)            }
[2241](https://docs.rs#2241)            sum += correction;
[2242](https://docs.rs#2242)            nq_pow *= nq.powf(-2.0);
[2243](https://docs.rs#2243)            // Rising factorial (s)(s+1)...(s+2k+1)
[2244](https://docs.rs#2244)            let kf = k as f64;
[2245](https://docs.rs#2245)            spow *= (s + 2.0 * kf + 1.0) * (s + 2.0 * kf + 2.0);
[2246](https://docs.rs#2246)        }
[2247](https://docs.rs#2247)        sum
[2248](https://docs.rs#2248)    }
[2249](https://docs.rs#2249)
[2250](https://docs.rs#2250)    fn euler_maclaurin(s: f64) -> f64 {
[2251](https://docs.rs#2251)        euler_maclaurin_hurwitz(s, 1.0)
[2252](https://docs.rs#2252)    }
[2253](https://docs.rs#2253)
[2254](https://docs.rs#2254)    // Euler transform of Dirichlet eta η(s) = Σ_{k=0}^∞ (-1)^k (k+1)^{-s}
[2255](https://docs.rs#2255)    // Forward-difference acceleration: η = Σ_{n=0}^N (Δ^n a)_0 / 2^{n+1}
[2256](https://docs.rs#2256)    // where a_k = (k+1)^{-s}. Requires O(N²) ops but N=60 → <1e-17 error.
[2257](https://docs.rs#2257)    fn euler_eta(s: f64) -> f64 {
[2258](https://docs.rs#2258)        const N: usize = 60;
[2259](https://docs.rs#2259)        let mut d: Vec<f64> = (0..=N).map(|k| (k as f64 + 1.0).powf(-s)).collect();
[2260](https://docs.rs#2260)        let mut sum = d[0] * 0.5;
[2261](https://docs.rs#2261)        for k in 1..=N {
[2262](https://docs.rs#2262)            let remain = N + 1 - k;
[2263](https://docs.rs#2263)            for j in 0..remain {
[2264](https://docs.rs#2264)                d[j] = d[j + 1] - d[j];
[2265](https://docs.rs#2265)            }
[2266](https://docs.rs#2266)            sum += d[0] / (2.0_f64.powi(k as i32 + 1));
[2267](https://docs.rs#2267)        }
[2268](https://docs.rs#2268)        sum
[2269](https://docs.rs#2269)    }
[2270](https://docs.rs#2270)}
[2271](https://docs.rs#2271)
[2272](https://docs.rs#2272)// ============================================================================
[2273](https://docs.rs#2273)// FRESNEL INTEGRALS
[2274](https://docs.rs#2274)// ============================================================================
[2275](https://docs.rs#2275)
[2276](https://docs.rs#2276)/// Fresnel integrals S(x) and C(x).
[2277](https://docs.rs#2277)pub mod fresnel_funcs {
[2278](https://docs.rs#2278)
[2279](https://docs.rs#2279)    /// Compute the Fresnel integrals S(x) and C(x).
[2280](https://docs.rs#2280)    ///
[2281](https://docs.rs#2281)    /// Returns `(S(x), C(x))` where:
[2282](https://docs.rs#2282)    /// - S(x) = ∫₀ˣ sin(πt²/2) dt
[2283](https://docs.rs#2283)    /// - C(x) = ∫₀ˣ cos(πt²/2) dt
[2284](https://docs.rs#2284)    ///
[2285](https://docs.rs#2285)    /// Uses power series for |x| ≤ 1.5 and asymptotic expansion for |x| > 1.5.
[2286](https://docs.rs#2286)    ///
[2287](https://docs.rs#2287)    /// # Invariants
[2288](https://docs.rs#2288)    /// - S(0) = C(0) = 0
[2289](https://docs.rs#2289)    /// - lim_{x→∞} S(x) = lim_{x→∞} C(x) = 1/2
[2290](https://docs.rs#2290)    ///
[2291](https://docs.rs#2291)    /// # References
[2292](https://docs.rs#2292)    /// - Abramowitz & Stegun §7.3. DOI: 10.6028/jres.069b.001
[2293](https://docs.rs#2293)    /// - NIST DLMF §7.2.
[2294](https://docs.rs#2294)    pub fn fresnel(x: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
[2295](https://docs.rs#2295)        if x == 0.0 {
[2296](https://docs.rs#2296)            return (0.0, 0.0);
[2297](https://docs.rs#2297)        }
[2298](https://docs.rs#2298)        let ax = x.abs();
[2299](https://docs.rs#2299)        // Power series for small x; asymptotic for x >= 2.5 (where g-series converges)
[2300](https://docs.rs#2300)        let (s, c) = if ax < 2.5 {
[2301](https://docs.rs#2301)            fresnel_series(ax)
[2302](https://docs.rs#2302)        } else {
[2303](https://docs.rs#2303)            fresnel_asymptotic(ax)
[2304](https://docs.rs#2304)        };
[2305](https://docs.rs#2305)        // Both S and C are odd functions
[2306](https://docs.rs#2306)        if x < 0.0 { (-s, -c) } else { (s, c) }
[2307](https://docs.rs#2307)    }
[2308](https://docs.rs#2308)
[2309](https://docs.rs#2309)    // Power series (A&S 7.3.11–12):
[2310](https://docs.rs#2310)    // S(x) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ (-1)^n (π/2)^{2n+1} x^{4n+3} / ((4n+3)(2n+1)!)
[2311](https://docs.rs#2311)    // C(x) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ (-1)^n (π/2)^{2n}   x^{4n+1} / ((4n+1)(2n)!)
[2312](https://docs.rs#2312)    // Power series via iterative term ratios — no factorial overflow.
[2313](https://docs.rs#2313)    // S: t_{n+1}/t_n = -(pi/2)^2 x^4 (4n+3) / ((4n+7)(2n+3)(2n+2))
[2314](https://docs.rs#2314)    // C: t_{n+1}/t_n = -(pi/2)^2 x^4 (4n+1) / ((4n+5)(2n+2)(2n+1))
[2315](https://docs.rs#2315)    fn fresnel_series(x: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
[2316](https://docs.rs#2316)        let pih2 = std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2 * std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
[2317](https://docs.rs#2317)        let neg_x4_pih2 = -(x * x * x * x) * pih2;
[2318](https://docs.rs#2318)
[2319](https://docs.rs#2319)        // S(x): first term = (pi/2) x^3 / 3
[2320](https://docs.rs#2320)        let mut s_term = std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2 * x * x * x / 3.0;
[2321](https://docs.rs#2321)        let mut s_sum = s_term;
[2322](https://docs.rs#2322)        for n in 0_usize..100 {
[2323](https://docs.rs#2323)            let nf = n as f64;
[2324](https://docs.rs#2324)            s_term *= neg_x4_pih2 * (4.0 * nf + 3.0)
[2325](https://docs.rs#2325)                / ((4.0 * nf + 7.0) * (2.0 * nf + 3.0) * (2.0 * nf + 2.0));
[2326](https://docs.rs#2326)            s_sum += s_term;
[2327](https://docs.rs#2327)            if s_term.abs() < 1e-16 * s_sum.abs().max(1e-300) || !s_sum.is_finite() {
[2328](https://docs.rs#2328)                break;
[2329](https://docs.rs#2329)            }
[2330](https://docs.rs#2330)        }
[2331](https://docs.rs#2331)
[2332](https://docs.rs#2332)        // C(x): first term = x
[2333](https://docs.rs#2333)        let mut c_term = x;
[2334](https://docs.rs#2334)        let mut c_sum = c_term;
[2335](https://docs.rs#2335)        for n in 0_usize..100 {
[2336](https://docs.rs#2336)            let nf = n as f64;
[2337](https://docs.rs#2337)            c_term *= neg_x4_pih2 * (4.0 * nf + 1.0)
[2338](https://docs.rs#2338)                / ((4.0 * nf + 5.0) * (2.0 * nf + 2.0) * (2.0 * nf + 1.0));
[2339](https://docs.rs#2339)            c_sum += c_term;
[2340](https://docs.rs#2340)            if c_term.abs() < 1e-16 * c_sum.abs().max(1e-300) || !c_sum.is_finite() {
[2341](https://docs.rs#2341)                break;
[2342](https://docs.rs#2342)            }
[2343](https://docs.rs#2343)        }
[2344](https://docs.rs#2344)        (s_sum, c_sum)
[2345](https://docs.rs#2345)    }
[2346](https://docs.rs#2346)
[2347](https://docs.rs#2347)    // Asymptotic expansion (A&S 7.3.23–24):
[2348](https://docs.rs#2348)    // f(x) = 1/(πx)[1 - 1·3/(πx²)² + ...]
[2349](https://docs.rs#2349)    // g(x) = 1/(πx²)[1 - 1·3·5·7/(πx²)² + ...]
[2350](https://docs.rs#2350)    // C(x) ≈ 1/2 + f(x)·sin(θ) - g(x)·cos(θ)    (θ = πx²/2)
[2351](https://docs.rs#2351)    // S(x) ≈ 1/2 - f(x)·cos(θ) - g(x)·sin(θ)
[2352](https://docs.rs#2352)    // Asymptotic expansion (A&S 7.3.23-24), accurate for x >= 2.5.
[2353](https://docs.rs#2353)    //
[2354](https://docs.rs#2354)    // f(x) = (1/(pi*x))  * f_sum   f_sum: term ratio = -(4n+1)(4n+3)/(pi*x^2)^2
[2355](https://docs.rs#2355)    // g(x) = (1/(pi^2*x^3)) * g_sum  g_sum: term ratio = -(4n+3)(4n+5)/(pi*x^2)^2
[2356](https://docs.rs#2356)    //
[2357](https://docs.rs#2357)    // C(x) = 1/2 + f*sin(theta) - g*cos(theta)
[2358](https://docs.rs#2358)    // S(x) = 1/2 - f*cos(theta) - g*sin(theta)   (theta = pi*x^2/2)
[2359](https://docs.rs#2359)    //
[2360](https://docs.rs#2360)    // Optimal truncation: stop when |next_term| >= |current_term|.
[2361](https://docs.rs#2361)    fn fresnel_asymptotic(x: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
[2362](https://docs.rs#2362)        let theta = std::f64::consts::PI * x * x / 2.0;
[2363](https://docs.rs#2363)        let (sin_th, cos_th) = theta.sin_cos();
[2364](https://docs.rs#2364)        let pix2_sq = (std::f64::consts::PI * x * x).powi(2); // (pi*x^2)^2
[2365](https://docs.rs#2365)
[2366](https://docs.rs#2366)        let mut f_term = 1.0_f64;
[2367](https://docs.rs#2367)        let mut f_sum = 1.0_f64;
[2368](https://docs.rs#2368)        for n in 0_usize..25 {
[2369](https://docs.rs#2369)            let nf = n as f64;
[2370](https://docs.rs#2370)            let next = f_term * (-(4.0 * nf + 1.0) * (4.0 * nf + 3.0)) / pix2_sq;
[2371](https://docs.rs#2371)            if next.abs() >= f_term.abs() {
[2372](https://docs.rs#2372)                break;
[2373](https://docs.rs#2373)            }
[2374](https://docs.rs#2374)            f_term = next;
[2375](https://docs.rs#2375)            f_sum += f_term;
[2376](https://docs.rs#2376)        }
[2377](https://docs.rs#2377)
[2378](https://docs.rs#2378)        let mut g_term = 1.0_f64;
[2379](https://docs.rs#2379)        let mut g_sum = 1.0_f64;
[2380](https://docs.rs#2380)        for n in 0_usize..25 {
[2381](https://docs.rs#2381)            let nf = n as f64;
[2382](https://docs.rs#2382)            let next = g_term * (-(4.0 * nf + 3.0) * (4.0 * nf + 5.0)) / pix2_sq;
[2383](https://docs.rs#2383)            if next.abs() >= g_term.abs() {
[2384](https://docs.rs#2384)                break;
[2385](https://docs.rs#2385)            }
[2386](https://docs.rs#2386)            g_term = next;
[2387](https://docs.rs#2387)            g_sum += g_term;
[2388](https://docs.rs#2388)        }
[2389](https://docs.rs#2389)
[2390](https://docs.rs#2390)        let pi = std::f64::consts::PI;
[2391](https://docs.rs#2391)        let f_val = f_sum / (pi * x);
[2392](https://docs.rs#2392)        let g_val = g_sum / (pi * pi * x * x * x);
[2393](https://docs.rs#2393)
[2394](https://docs.rs#2394)        let c = 0.5 + f_val * sin_th - g_val * cos_th;
[2395](https://docs.rs#2395)        let s = 0.5 - f_val * cos_th - g_val * sin_th;
[2396](https://docs.rs#2396)        (s, c)
[2397](https://docs.rs#2397)    }
[2398](https://docs.rs#2398)}
[2399](https://docs.rs#2399)
[2400](https://docs.rs#2400)// ============================================================================
[2401](https://docs.rs#2401)// HYPERGEOMETRIC FUNCTIONS
[2402](https://docs.rs#2402)// ============================================================================
[2403](https://docs.rs#2403)
[2404](https://docs.rs#2404)/// Hypergeometric functions ₁F₁, ₂F₁.
[2405](https://docs.rs#2405)pub mod hypergeom {
[2406](https://docs.rs#2406)    use super::{SpecialError, SpecialResult};
[2407](https://docs.rs#2407)
[2408](https://docs.rs#2408)    /// Confluent hypergeometric function (Kummer) ₁F₁(a; b; z).
[2409](https://docs.rs#2409)    ///
[2410](https://docs.rs#2410)    /// ₁F₁(a;b;z) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ (a)_n z^n / ((b)_n n!)
[2411](https://docs.rs#2411)    ///
[2412](https://docs.rs#2412)    /// For large negative z, uses Kummer's transform: ₁F₁(a;b;z) = eᶻ·₁F₁(b-a;b;-z)
[2413](https://docs.rs#2413)    /// to avoid catastrophic cancellation.
[2414](https://docs.rs#2414)    ///
[2415](https://docs.rs#2415)    /// # Closed forms (for testing)
[2416](https://docs.rs#2416)    /// - ₁F₁(a;a;z) = eᶻ
[2417](https://docs.rs#2417)    /// - ₁F₁(1;2;z) = (eᶻ−1)/z
[2418](https://docs.rs#2418)    ///
[2419](https://docs.rs#2419)    /// # References
[2420](https://docs.rs#2420)    /// - NIST DLMF §13. DOI: 10.6028/jres.069b.001
[2421](https://docs.rs#2421)    /// - Abramowitz & Stegun §13.
[2422](https://docs.rs#2422)    pub fn hyp1f1(a: f64, b: f64, z: f64) -> SpecialResult<f64> {
[2423](https://docs.rs#2423)        if b <= 0.0 && b.floor() == b {
[2424](https://docs.rs#2424)            return Err(SpecialError::DomainError(
[2425](https://docs.rs#2425)                format!("hyp1f1: b={b} is a non-positive integer (pole)"),
[2426](https://docs.rs#2426)            ));
[2427](https://docs.rs#2427)        }
[2428](https://docs.rs#2428)        if a == b {
[2429](https://docs.rs#2429)            return Ok(z.exp()); // closed form
[2430](https://docs.rs#2430)        }
[2431](https://docs.rs#2431)        if z == 0.0 {
[2432](https://docs.rs#2432)            return Ok(1.0);
[2433](https://docs.rs#2433)        }
[2434](https://docs.rs#2434)
[2435](https://docs.rs#2435)        // For large negative z use Kummer transform to avoid cancellation:
[2436](https://docs.rs#2436)        // ₁F₁(a;b;z) = eᶻ · ₁F₁(b-a;b;-z)
[2437](https://docs.rs#2437)        if z < -10.0 {
[2438](https://docs.rs#2438)            let result = hyp1f1_series(b - a, b, -z)?;
[2439](https://docs.rs#2439)            return Ok(z.exp() * result);
[2440](https://docs.rs#2440)        }
[2441](https://docs.rs#2441)
[2442](https://docs.rs#2442)        hyp1f1_series(a, b, z)
[2443](https://docs.rs#2443)    }
[2444](https://docs.rs#2444)
[2445](https://docs.rs#2445)    fn hyp1f1_series(a: f64, b: f64, z: f64) -> SpecialResult<f64> {
[2446](https://docs.rs#2446)        let mut term = 1.0_f64;
[2447](https://docs.rs#2447)        let mut sum = 1.0_f64;
[2448](https://docs.rs#2448)        for n in 1_usize..500 {
[2449](https://docs.rs#2449)            let nf = n as f64;
[2450](https://docs.rs#2450)            term *= (a + nf - 1.0) * z / ((b + nf - 1.0) * nf);
[2451](https://docs.rs#2451)            sum += term;
[2452](https://docs.rs#2452)            if term.abs() < 1e-16 * sum.abs().max(1e-300) {
[2453](https://docs.rs#2453)                return Ok(sum);
[2454](https://docs.rs#2454)            }
[2455](https://docs.rs#2455)            if !sum.is_finite() {
[2456](https://docs.rs#2456)                return Err(SpecialError::OverflowError(
[2457](https://docs.rs#2457)                    format!("hyp1f1({a},{b},{z}): series overflowed"),
[2458](https://docs.rs#2458)                ));
[2459](https://docs.rs#2459)            }
[2460](https://docs.rs#2460)        }
[2461](https://docs.rs#2461)        Err(SpecialError::ConvergenceError(
[2462](https://docs.rs#2462)            format!("hyp1f1({a},{b},{z}): series did not converge in 500 terms"),
[2463](https://docs.rs#2463)        ))
[2464](https://docs.rs#2464)    }
[2465](https://docs.rs#2465)
[2466](https://docs.rs#2466)    /// Gauss hypergeometric function ₂F₁(a, b; c; z) for real z ∈ (−1, 1).
[2467](https://docs.rs#2467)    ///
[2468](https://docs.rs#2468)    /// ₂F₁(a,b;c;z) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ (a)_n(b)_n z^n / ((c)_n n!)
[2469](https://docs.rs#2469)    ///
[2470](https://docs.rs#2470)    /// Convergence radius |z| < 1. Returns `DomainError` for |z| ≥ 1.
[2471](https://docs.rs#2471)    ///
[2472](https://docs.rs#2472)    /// # Closed forms
[2473](https://docs.rs#2473)    /// - ₂F₁(1,1;2;z) = −ln(1−z)/z
[2474](https://docs.rs#2474)    /// - ₂F₁(a,b;b;z) = (1−z)^{−a}
[2475](https://docs.rs#2475)    ///
[2476](https://docs.rs#2476)    /// # Scope
[2477](https://docs.rs#2477)    /// Real z ∈ (−1, 1). Complex or |z|≥1 not supported; use mpmath for those cases.
[2478](https://docs.rs#2478)    ///
[2479](https://docs.rs#2479)    /// # References
[2480](https://docs.rs#2480)    /// - NIST DLMF §15. DOI: 10.6028/jres.069b.001
[2481](https://docs.rs#2481)    /// - Abramowitz & Stegun §15.
[2482](https://docs.rs#2482)    pub fn hyp2f1(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64, z: f64) -> SpecialResult<f64> {
[2483](https://docs.rs#2483)        if c <= 0.0 && c.floor() == c {
[2484](https://docs.rs#2484)            return Err(SpecialError::DomainError(
[2485](https://docs.rs#2485)                format!("hyp2f1: c={c} is a non-positive integer (pole)"),
[2486](https://docs.rs#2486)            ));
[2487](https://docs.rs#2487)        }
[2488](https://docs.rs#2488)        if z.abs() >= 1.0 {
[2489](https://docs.rs#2489)            return Err(SpecialError::DomainError(
[2490](https://docs.rs#2490)                format!("hyp2f1: |z|={} >= 1; series diverges (use mpmath for analytic continuation)", z.abs())
[2491](https://docs.rs#2491)            ));
[2492](https://docs.rs#2492)        }
[2493](https://docs.rs#2493)        if z == 0.0 {
[2494](https://docs.rs#2494)            return Ok(1.0);
[2495](https://docs.rs#2495)        }
[2496](https://docs.rs#2496)        // Closed form: ₂F₁(a,b;b;z) = (1-z)^{-a}
[2497](https://docs.rs#2497)        if (b - c).abs() < 1e-14 {
[2498](https://docs.rs#2498)            return Ok((1.0 - z).powf(-a));
[2499](https://docs.rs#2499)        }
[2500](https://docs.rs#2500)
[2501](https://docs.rs#2501)        hyp2f1_series(a, b, c, z)
[2502](https://docs.rs#2502)    }
[2503](https://docs.rs#2503)
[2504](https://docs.rs#2504)    fn hyp2f1_series(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64, z: f64) -> SpecialResult<f64> {
[2505](https://docs.rs#2505)        let mut term = 1.0_f64;
[2506](https://docs.rs#2506)        let mut sum = 1.0_f64;
[2507](https://docs.rs#2507)        for n in 1_usize..500 {
[2508](https://docs.rs#2508)            let nf = n as f64;
[2509](https://docs.rs#2509)            term *= (a + nf - 1.0) * (b + nf - 1.0) * z / ((c + nf - 1.0) * nf);
[2510](https://docs.rs#2510)            sum += term;
[2511](https://docs.rs#2511)            if term.abs() < 1e-16 * sum.abs().max(1e-300) {
[2512](https://docs.rs#2512)                return Ok(sum);
[2513](https://docs.rs#2513)            }
[2514](https://docs.rs#2514)            if !sum.is_finite() {
[2515](https://docs.rs#2515)                return Err(SpecialError::OverflowError(
[2516](https://docs.rs#2516)                    format!("hyp2f1({a},{b},{c},{z}): series overflowed"),
[2517](https://docs.rs#2517)                ));
[2518](https://docs.rs#2518)            }
[2519](https://docs.rs#2519)        }
[2520](https://docs.rs#2520)        // For |z| close to 1 the series may be slow but should converge
[2521](https://docs.rs#2521)        Err(SpecialError::ConvergenceError(
[2522](https://docs.rs#2522)            format!("hyp2f1({a},{b},{c},{z}): series did not converge in 500 terms"),
[2523](https://docs.rs#2523)        ))
[2524](https://docs.rs#2524)    }
[2525](https://docs.rs#2525)}
[2526](https://docs.rs#2526)
[2527](https://docs.rs#2527)// ============================================================================
[2528](https://docs.rs#2528)// STRUVE FUNCTIONS
[2529](https://docs.rs#2529)// ============================================================================
[2530](https://docs.rs#2530)
[2531](https://docs.rs#2531)/// Struve H_ν(x) and modified Struve L_ν(x) functions.
[2532](https://docs.rs#2532)///
[2533](https://docs.rs#2533)/// Power series (DLMF §11.2.2) for |x| ≤ 20; asymptotic expansion (DLMF §11.6)
[2534](https://docs.rs#2534)/// for x > 20. Accurate for ν ≥ −3/2; returns `NAN` for non-integer ν with x < 0.
[2535](https://docs.rs#2535)pub mod struve {
[2536](https://docs.rs#2536)    use super::*;
[2537](https://docs.rs#2537)    use std::f64::consts::PI;
[2538](https://docs.rs#2538)
[2539](https://docs.rs#2539)    // Sign of Γ(a) for non-pole a: alternates by interval (-k, -k+1).
[2540](https://docs.rs#2540)    fn gamma_sign(a: f64) -> f64 {
[2541](https://docs.rs#2541)        if a > 0.0 {
[2542](https://docs.rs#2542)            1.0
[2543](https://docs.rs#2543)        } else if a == a.floor() {
[2544](https://docs.rs#2544)            0.0 // pole — caller treats as 1/Γ(a) = 0
[2545](https://docs.rs#2545)        } else {
[2546](https://docs.rs#2546)            let k = (-a).ceil() as i64; // a in (−k, −k+1)
[2547](https://docs.rs#2547)            if k % 2 == 0 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 }
[2548](https://docs.rs#2548)        }
[2549](https://docs.rs#2549)    }
[2550](https://docs.rs#2550)
[2551](https://docs.rs#2551)    // Power series for H_ν(x), x > 0.
[2552](https://docs.rs#2552)    // H_ν(x) = t0 · Σ_{m≥0} (-1)^m r_m  where t0=(x/2)^{ν+1}/(Γ(3/2)Γ(ν+3/2)).
[2553](https://docs.rs#2553)    // Ratio: r_{m+1}/r_m = −(x/2)² / ((m+3/2)(m+ν+3/2)).
[2554](https://docs.rs#2554)    fn h_series(v: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[2555](https://docs.rs#2555)        let hx = x / 2.0;
[2556](https://docs.rs#2556)        let a = v + 1.5;
[2557](https://docs.rs#2557)        let ln_t0 = (v + 1.0) * hx.ln() - lgamma(1.5) - lgamma(a);
[2558](https://docs.rs#2558)        if !ln_t0.is_finite() {
[2559](https://docs.rs#2559)            return 0.0;
[2560](https://docs.rs#2560)        }
[2561](https://docs.rs#2561)        let t0 = gamma_sign(a) * ln_t0.exp();
[2562](https://docs.rs#2562)        if t0 == 0.0 {
[2563](https://docs.rs#2563)            return 0.0;
[2564](https://docs.rs#2564)        }
[2565](https://docs.rs#2565)        let hx2 = hx * hx;
[2566](https://docs.rs#2566)        let mut r = 1.0_f64;
[2567](https://docs.rs#2567)        let mut sum = 1.0_f64;
[2568](https://docs.rs#2568)        for m in 0_u32..500 {
[2569](https://docs.rs#2569)            let mf = m as f64;
[2570](https://docs.rs#2570)            let d = (mf + 1.5) * (mf + v + 1.5);
[2571](https://docs.rs#2571)            if d == 0.0 {
[2572](https://docs.rs#2572)                break;
[2573](https://docs.rs#2573)            }
[2574](https://docs.rs#2574)            r *= -hx2 / d;
[2575](https://docs.rs#2575)            if !r.is_finite() {
[2576](https://docs.rs#2576)                break;
[2577](https://docs.rs#2577)            }
[2578](https://docs.rs#2578)            let prev = sum;
[2579](https://docs.rs#2579)            sum += r;
[2580](https://docs.rs#2580)            if (sum - prev).abs() <= 1e-16 * sum.abs() {
[2581](https://docs.rs#2581)                break;
[2582](https://docs.rs#2582)            }
[2583](https://docs.rs#2583)        }
[2584](https://docs.rs#2584)        t0 * sum
[2585](https://docs.rs#2585)    }
[2586](https://docs.rs#2586)
[2587](https://docs.rs#2587)    // Power series for L_ν(x), x > 0.  All positive terms — no cancellation.
[2588](https://docs.rs#2588)    // Same structure as H_ν but ratio is +(x/2)²/… (no alternating sign).
[2589](https://docs.rs#2589)    fn l_series(v: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[2590](https://docs.rs#2590)        let hx = x / 2.0;
[2591](https://docs.rs#2591)        let a = v + 1.5;
[2592](https://docs.rs#2592)        let ln_t0 = (v + 1.0) * hx.ln() - lgamma(1.5) - lgamma(a);
[2593](https://docs.rs#2593)        if !ln_t0.is_finite() {
[2594](https://docs.rs#2594)            return 0.0;
[2595](https://docs.rs#2595)        }
[2596](https://docs.rs#2596)        let t0 = gamma_sign(a) * ln_t0.exp();
[2597](https://docs.rs#2597)        if t0 == 0.0 {
[2598](https://docs.rs#2598)            return 0.0;
[2599](https://docs.rs#2599)        }
[2600](https://docs.rs#2600)        let hx2 = hx * hx;
[2601](https://docs.rs#2601)        let mut r = 1.0_f64;
[2602](https://docs.rs#2602)        let mut sum = 1.0_f64;
[2603](https://docs.rs#2603)        for m in 0_u32..500 {
[2604](https://docs.rs#2604)            let mf = m as f64;
[2605](https://docs.rs#2605)            let d = (mf + 1.5) * (mf + v + 1.5);
[2606](https://docs.rs#2606)            if d == 0.0 {
[2607](https://docs.rs#2607)                break;
[2608](https://docs.rs#2608)            }
[2609](https://docs.rs#2609)            r *= hx2 / d;
[2610](https://docs.rs#2610)            if !r.is_finite() {
[2611](https://docs.rs#2611)                break;
[2612](https://docs.rs#2612)            }
[2613](https://docs.rs#2613)            let prev = sum;
[2614](https://docs.rs#2614)            sum += r;
[2615](https://docs.rs#2615)            if (sum - prev).abs() <= 1e-16 * sum.abs() {
[2616](https://docs.rs#2616)                break;
[2617](https://docs.rs#2617)            }
[2618](https://docs.rs#2618)        }
[2619](https://docs.rs#2619)        t0 * sum
[2620](https://docs.rs#2620)    }
[2621](https://docs.rs#2621)
[2622](https://docs.rs#2622)    // Asymptotic correction c(ν,x) (DLMF §11.6.1/2):
[2623](https://docs.rs#2623)    //   H_ν(x) = Y_ν(x) + c,    L_ν(x) = I_ν(x) − c.
[2624](https://docs.rs#2624)    //
[2625](https://docs.rs#2625)    // term_0 = Γ(½)/Γ(ν+½) · (x/2)^{ν−1}
[2626](https://docs.rs#2626)    // term_{k+1} = term_k · (k+½)(ν−k−½) / (x/2)²
[2627](https://docs.rs#2627)    // c = (1/π) Σ term_k   (stop when |term| starts growing).
[2628](https://docs.rs#2628)    fn asymptotic_correction(v: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[2629](https://docs.rs#2629)        let hx = x / 2.0;
[2630](https://docs.rs#2630)        let gv = gamma(v + 0.5);
[2631](https://docs.rs#2631)        if !gv.is_finite() || gv == 0.0 {
[2632](https://docs.rs#2632)            return 0.0; // 1/Γ(v+½)=0 → correction is zero (H_ν=Y_ν exactly)
[2633](https://docs.rs#2633)        }
[2634](https://docs.rs#2634)        let mut term = PI.sqrt() * hx.powf(v - 1.0) / gv;
[2635](https://docs.rs#2635)        if !term.is_finite() {
[2636](https://docs.rs#2636)            return 0.0;
[2637](https://docs.rs#2637)        }
[2638](https://docs.rs#2638)        let hx2 = hx * hx;
[2639](https://docs.rs#2639)        let mut sum = 0.0_f64;
[2640](https://docs.rs#2640)        let mut prev_abs = f64::INFINITY;
[2641](https://docs.rs#2641)        for k in 0_u32..60 {
[2642](https://docs.rs#2642)            let abs_t = term.abs();
[2643](https://docs.rs#2643)            if abs_t >= prev_abs {
[2644](https://docs.rs#2644)                break; // asymptotic series diverging — truncate
[2645](https://docs.rs#2645)            }
[2646](https://docs.rs#2646)            sum += term;
[2647](https://docs.rs#2647)            prev_abs = abs_t;
[2648](https://docs.rs#2648)            let kf = k as f64;
[2649](https://docs.rs#2649)            term *= (kf + 0.5) * (v - kf - 0.5) / hx2;
[2650](https://docs.rs#2650)            if !term.is_finite() {
[2651](https://docs.rs#2651)                break;
[2652](https://docs.rs#2652)            }
[2653](https://docs.rs#2653)        }
[2654](https://docs.rs#2654)        sum / PI
[2655](https://docs.rs#2655)    }
[2656](https://docs.rs#2656)
[2657](https://docs.rs#2657)    /// Struve H function H_ν(x) (DLMF §11.2).
[2658](https://docs.rs#2658)    ///
[2659](https://docs.rs#2659)    /// Returns `NAN` for `x < 0` with non-integer ν.
[2660](https://docs.rs#2660)    pub fn struve_h(v: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[2661](https://docs.rs#2661)        if x == 0.0 {
[2662](https://docs.rs#2662)            return 0.0;
[2663](https://docs.rs#2663)        }
[2664](https://docs.rs#2664)        if x < 0.0 {
[2665](https://docs.rs#2665)            if (v.round() - v).abs() < 1e-10 {
[2666](https://docs.rs#2666)                // H_n(−x) = (−1)^{n+1} H_n(x)  (series derivation)
[2667](https://docs.rs#2667)                let n = v.round() as i64;
[2668](https://docs.rs#2668)                let sign = if n % 2 == 0 { -1.0_f64 } else { 1.0_f64 };
[2669](https://docs.rs#2669)                return sign * struve_h(v, -x);
[2670](https://docs.rs#2670)            }
[2671](https://docs.rs#2671)            return f64::NAN;
[2672](https://docs.rs#2672)        }
[2673](https://docs.rs#2673)        if x <= 20.0 {
[2674](https://docs.rs#2674)            h_series(v, x)
[2675](https://docs.rs#2675)        } else {
[2676](https://docs.rs#2676)            bessel::yv(v, x) + asymptotic_correction(v, x)
[2677](https://docs.rs#2677)        }
[2678](https://docs.rs#2678)    }
[2679](https://docs.rs#2679)
[2680](https://docs.rs#2680)    /// Modified Struve L function L_ν(x) (DLMF §11.2).
[2681](https://docs.rs#2681)    ///
[2682](https://docs.rs#2682)    /// Returns `NAN` for `x < 0` with non-integer ν.
[2683](https://docs.rs#2683)    pub fn struve_l(v: f64, x: f64) -> f64 {
[2684](https://docs.rs#2684)        if x == 0.0 {
[2685](https://docs.rs#2685)            return 0.0;
[2686](https://docs.rs#2686)        }
[2687](https://docs.rs#2687)        if x < 0.0 {
[2688](https://docs.rs#2688)            if (v.round() - v).abs() < 1e-10 {
[2689](https://docs.rs#2689)                // L_n(−x) = (−1)^{n+1} L_n(x)  (same parity as H_n)
[2690](https://docs.rs#2690)                let n = v.round() as i64;
[2691](https://docs.rs#2691)                let sign = if n % 2 == 0 { -1.0_f64 } else { 1.0_f64 };
[2692](https://docs.rs#2692)                return sign * struve_l(v, -x);
[2693](https://docs.rs#2693)            }
[2694](https://docs.rs#2694)            return f64::NAN;
[2695](https://docs.rs#2695)        }
[2696](https://docs.rs#2696)        if x <= 20.0 {
[2697](https://docs.rs#2697)            l_series(v, x)
[2698](https://docs.rs#2698)        } else {
[2699](https://docs.rs#2699)            bessel::iv(v, x) - asymptotic_correction(v, x)
[2700](https://docs.rs#2700)        }
[2701](https://docs.rs#2701)    }

[2747](https://docs.rs#2747)// TESTS
